An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved high-voltage stability and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%.

title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a solid electrolyte layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The material comprises Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 500 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. Specific examples are Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the solid electrolyte at the negative electrode is suppressed and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 10 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 125 cycles or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable thio-LISICON crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of P2O5 is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 60% to 95%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours.

title: Hafnium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON solid electrolyte stable above 5 V and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved ionic conductivity at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.4 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 100 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium indium chloride ceramic ion conductor with orthorhombic structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.02 to 0.25, and a method for producing the same are provided. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The median particle diameter D50 is 3 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tantalum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 89% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1150 degrees C, and the resulting density is 92%. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.05 <= v <= 0.4, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The ion-conductive solid shows an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 2 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 2 cm3/g. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 80% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a tin substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3YCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The Li3InCl6, Li2ZrO3, and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The coating layer has an average thickness of 3 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The material comprises Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium fluoride (LiF). Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Non-aqueous electrolyte with a fluorinated solvent for a high voltage lithium battery
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide dissolved in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite as an additive in an amount of 3 wt%. The stable passivation film formed by tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 1000 cycles. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. The cell retains 88% of its capacity after 1000 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks. The capacity retention of 88% after 1000 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.4 V. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. A pouch type lithium ion battery comprising a nickel-rich positive electrode, a graphite negative electrode, and the electrolyte is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate; and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 3 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with tungsten and sintered with Li2CO3 is described. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. When v is 0.4, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 12 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 93% or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt%. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO and Li2ZrO3 material. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.15 to 0.5, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the grain boundary resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.15 <= v <= 0.5, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 94% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in ethyl acetate to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The suspension concentration is 15 wt%, the reaction temperature is 60 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the ionic conductivity of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for preparing the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.7 V or more is described. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved sinterability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ion-conductive solid with trigonal structure and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, YBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.3 V versus Li/Li+. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF material. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an oxygen-rich surface region is described. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The oxygen content of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 40 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 3.1 mS/cm or more. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 24 hours is 75% or more.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2WO4 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The cubic Li6PS5X structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and Li3InCl6. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Solvent-free self-supporting sulfide ion-conductive solid sheet bound by a fibrillated fluoropolymer network and method of forming the same
abstract: A self-supporting sheet comprises particles of an argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid of the Li6PS5Cl type and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene binder in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 3 wt%, the binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without any solvent. The sheet is formed by kneading the powder and the binder under a shear rate of 200 s^-1 to 800 s^-1 at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C so that the binder is fibrillized, rolling the kneaded mass between a pair of rollers heated to 80 degrees C to 120 degrees C, and calendering the rolled film in at least three passes with a stepwise reduced roller gap to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 60 micrometers. The fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 300 nm, and the sheet has a porosity of 8% or less, a tensile strength of 1.5 MPa or more, and an ionic conductivity of 2.0 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Because no polar solvent contacts the sulfide, the conductivity of the powder is retained, and the sheet can be wound on a roll and laminated onto an electrode without a drying step. An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved sheet formability in production and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A self-supporting sheet comprising: particles of a sulfide ion-conductive solid having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene binder in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 3 wt% relative to the sheet, the binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles, wherein the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 300 nm, the sheet is free of a solvent, and the sheet has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 60 micrometers and a porosity of 8% or less.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: A garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body having an average grain size of 10 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. When v is 0.5, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.4 mS/cm. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the ionic conductivity of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.35 <= v <= 0.7.

title: Method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% and a viscosity of 3000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 50 micrometers and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The binder is polyisobutylene in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent anisole. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the layer shows improved ionic conductivity and a thin electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: An electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at -20 degrees C and a method of preparing it are described. The capacity retention of 90% after 1000 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without fluoroethylene carbonate. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.3 V. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 60 degrees C. The cell retains 90% of its capacity after 1000 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 60 degrees C for 4 weeks. The 1.2 M lithium tetrafluoroborate solution in ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.2 M and fluoroethylene carbonate as an additive.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The lithium borate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 5.5 mS/cm. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The low electronic conductivity of the Li6PS5Cl material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 70%. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the content of Li2O is 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide solid electrolyte in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 1.05 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. In the monoclinic structure, yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The zirconium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiNbO3 and Li6PS5Cl material. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours, the conductivity retention is 70%. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 60% or more.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3InCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3InCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with tantalum and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The total ionic conductivity is 0.28 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 91% or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. The Li2ZrO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The lithium tantalate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.8 nm to 40 nm.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved sinterability and ionic conductivity compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 12 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the solid electrolyte at the negative electrode is suppressed and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.3% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li2WO4 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3InCl6, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm.

title: Tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a nickel cermet anode and a yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a planar solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising unit cells with a yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte, metal interconnects, and a glass sealant. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the yttria-stabilized zirconia cell. A 8 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 8 micrometers. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 500 to 650 degrees C. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 500 to 650 degrees C. The stack shows stable operation over 100 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 500 to 650 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising yttria-stabilized zirconia and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 500 to 650 degrees C.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, LLZO, and LATP material. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 20 micrometers. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ion-conductive solid, and the layer shows improved sheet formability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.2 mS/cm. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 40 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing LiI. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. The content of LiI is 5 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and to a solid-state battery comprising the same. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 9.6 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. Compared with Li6PS5Br, the iodine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.5, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The ion-conductive solid is preferably beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material. The additive content is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, the stack pressure is 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa, and the critical current density is 4 mA/cm2. The magnesium additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. The additive comprises magnesium in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The method prevents short circuit and improves the cycle life and sheet formability without a thick protective layer.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.8% or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. Examples of the ion conductor include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved moisture stability and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 170 degrees C to 360 degrees C.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The resulting Li6PS5Cl material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.12 or less. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.3 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5.2 V. The low electronic conductivity of the LLZO and Li2ZrO3 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The oxide solid electrolyte enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.6 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 2 mol% to 40 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated therein. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The content of P2O5 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.3 mS/cm or more. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved ionic conductivity compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 20% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer that has a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s. The ion-conductive component may be Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material.
