The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The solid content is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, the viscosity is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.8 mS/cm or more.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-GeS2 glass. The resulting Li3PS4 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The content of GeS2 is 5 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.8 mS/cm or more. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 60% to 95%.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.9 mS/cm or more.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using nitrile butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 200 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. A lithium battery pack comprising 8 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 200 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 100 micrometers.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 100 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 200 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and lithium fluoride (LiF). The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl and LiF material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.4 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium erbium chloride solid electrolyte with monoclinic structure and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF). The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.9 micrometers to 9 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. After dehydration under vacuum at 250 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.6, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours. The Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours is 75% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a tin substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A solid electrolyte sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and an all-solid-state lithium battery including the sheet are described. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A precursor of the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 100 degrees C to form a continuous film. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The roll temperature is 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers after calendering. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The method shortens the process and improves the interfacial resistance and sheet formability of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 10% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The LiF, Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF), beta-Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.8% or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Crystallized sulfide glass ceramic ion conductor containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved electrochemical window compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%, and wherein the content of Li2O is 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.45, and wherein 1.3 <= a <= 1.7.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The Li6PS5Cl and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The lithium niobate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 90%. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 85% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.7 V or more.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which solid electrolyte particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. No solvent is used in the process, so the solid electrolyte does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A precursor of the LATP and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 30% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tungstate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6 and LiNbO3 material. The coating layer has an average thickness of 5 nm and a coverage of 90%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and method for producing the same
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 3.1 mS/cm. The low electronic conductivity of the Li6PS5Cl material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of LiI is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for preparing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The low electronic conductivity of the Li6PS5Cl material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better moisture stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein 0.35 <= y/a <= 0.65, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in 1,2-dimethoxyethane at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Heat treatment at 550 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coating layer has an average thickness of 15 nm and a coverage of 80%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 60% relative to uncoated particles. The lithium niobium tantalum oxide shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li3PS4 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. The Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, and wherein 1.3 <= a <= 1.7.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid arsenic-free antimony binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 10 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the sinterability are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours is 80% or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide ceramic ion conductor in which indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the high-voltage stability at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.47 mS/cm or more.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium erbium chloride solid electrolyte with trigonal structure for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which hafnium is substituted for part of the erbium in a lithium erbium chloride framework. Suitable compositions include lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. After dehydration under vacuum at 200 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. In the trigonal structure, erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with aluminum and sintered with LiF is described. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The total ionic conductivity is 0.42 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.24 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 0.2 micrometers to 12 micrometers, and wherein 0.31 <= v <= 1.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The Li3InCl6 and LiNbO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and lithium battery
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. An ionic conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.3 to 1.7. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein 1.3 <= a <= 1.7.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.1 mS/cm or more. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 100 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours is 55% or more.

title: Lithium borate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3BO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiTaO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. A solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A precursor of the Li2ZrO3 and Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved moisture stability and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium battery
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 1.8 mS/cm. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the content of GeS2 is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 4.5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 83% or more. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the sinterability is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 83% or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium zirconate and to a method for producing the same. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. After exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity retention is 80%. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The oxygen substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and Li3InCl6. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 70% or more are obtained. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 70% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less.

title: Dendrite-suppressing silver additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 4 mA/cm2. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the content of the silver additive is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.3 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state battery. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 100%.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer that has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s. The wet film is dried at 60 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The binder is styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The method further comprises a synthesis step in which a solvate complex is precipitated and heat-treated to obtain the powder. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The solid content is 40 wt% to 60 wt%, the viscosity is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. A solid-state battery using the layer shows improved sheet formability and a thin electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 40 wt% to 60 wt%.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Ag-C layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising an Ag-C inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium fluoride (LiF). Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 200 nm. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 200 cycles of stable plating and stripping. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The bilayer structure improves the dendrite suppression compared with a single inorganic layer.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 80 nm to 400 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.3% or more.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a zinc-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density.
