Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. A Coulombic efficiency of 99% or more and a critical current density of 1.5 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The additive comprises zinc in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved dendrite suppression and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the zinc additive is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 99% or more.

title: Method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The viscosity of 500 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The slurry has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved ionic conductivity and sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a Li3N inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The material comprises Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 300 nm. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 500 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.5% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 125 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 30 nm to 1800 nm.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 5 wt% to 20 wt%.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-LiI glass. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. Crystallization is performed at 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the content of LiI is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Ceramic ion conductor slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a ceramic ion conductor is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The binder is polyisobutylene in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent xylene. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C in an oven. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The solid content is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, the viscosity is 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1.3 mS/cm or more.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte and to a lithium battery including the same. The grain size is 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and the relative density is 89% or more after sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The method gives reproducible densification and improved sinterability at a lower cost.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 900 degrees C to 1250 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.24 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.01 <= v <= 0.7.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The roll temperature is 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers after calendering. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A lithium secondary battery using the sheet shows improved sheet formability and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.8 MPa or more.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 10 mol%. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. When v is 0.4, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Sintering is performed at 1150 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.25 <= v <= 0.6.

title: Lithium nitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The protective layer thickness is 200 nm to 1000 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.5% or more. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.2% or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 50 nm to 3000 nm.

title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which solid electrolyte particles are dispersed in heptane with a rubber binder and a dispersant. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and beta-Li3PS4. The binder content of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% gives a peel strength of 0.1 N/cm or more and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the cycle life of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 92%. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The oxide particles have a core of the perovskite-type LLTO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The widened electrochemical window improves the grain boundary resistance of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.9 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.21 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 5 mol%. When v is 0.4, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.6 mS/cm. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. A lithium excess of 5 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the sinterability of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.25 <= v <= 0.6, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 2 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Br6. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.2 to 0.45 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.47 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more.

title: tantalum solid electrolytic capacitor having a low equivalent series resistance
abstract: A conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor and a capacitor using the dispersion are provided. The capacitor shows improved heat resistance at 105 degrees C and can be mounted by reflow soldering. The dielectric oxide film is formed by anodizing the tantalum anode body in a phosphoric acid solution at a formation voltage of 2 to 4 times the rated voltage. The repair step reduces the leakage current and improves the reliability of the tantalum capacitor. The polypyrrole is doped with polystyrene sulfonate and has a particle size of 20 nm to 100 nm in the dispersion. The equivalent series resistance is 5 milliohms or less and the leakage current is 0.01 CV or less.
first_claim: 1. A conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising polypyrrole particles doped with polystyrene sulfonate, a polyhydric alcohol, and water, wherein the particles have a median diameter of 20 nm to 100 nm.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3YCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3YCl6 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3). An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The lithium yttrium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1 nm to 50 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte with orthorhombic structure and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. When z is 0.4, the conductivity is 3 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.5 V. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 and LiF material. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein 0 <= z <= 0.8, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Br6 and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of indium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.2 V. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF and Li3InCl6 material. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in ethyl propionate to give a sulfide ceramic ion conductor precursor. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using acetonitrile and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from acetonitrile, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 40 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the moisture stability of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The Li7P3S11 and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. With germanium substitution of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. Part of the titanium in the NASICON-type LATP phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 87% or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. Specific examples are Li3InCl6. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The Li3InCl6 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the ionic conductivity of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C.

title: Tungsten-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tungsten-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 94% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. Sintering is performed at 1230 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The dopant tungsten occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.35 to 0.7, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1230 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm and a relative density of 97%. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.35 <= v <= 0.7, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 94% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. The additive comprises lithium fluoride in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The Li3PS4, LiF, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The additive content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, the stack pressure is 10 MPa to 40 MPa, and the critical current density is 1 mA/cm2. The method prevents short circuit and improves the interfacial resistance without a thick protective layer.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 60 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 4 MPa to 100 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Zirconium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.8 V and method for producing the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more is described. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 85%. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The widened electrochemical window improves the ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 80% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and a film-forming additive
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 60 degrees C. The 1.0 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The combination of fluoroethylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.3 V. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.0 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. A pouch type lithium ion battery comprising a nickel-rich positive electrode, a graphite negative electrode, and the electrolyte is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate; and fluoroethylene carbonate in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using ethyl acetate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. Heat treatment at 550 degrees C after drying at 150 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the sinterability of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C.

title: Anode-supported solid oxide fuel cell having a thin scandia-stabilized zirconia electrolyte layer and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A solid oxide fuel cell includes a porous nickel-cermet anode support, a dense electrolyte layer comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia with a thickness of 15 micrometers or less, a diffusion barrier layer of doped ceria, and a perovskite cathode. The solid electrolyte layer of scandia-stabilized zirconia conducts oxide ions and separates the fuel from the air. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 95%. Hydrogen or reformed natural gas is supplied to the anode and air is supplied to the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode at 600 to 750 degrees C. The thin 15 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 1.5 W/cm2. Because the barrier layer prevents interfacial reaction with the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode, the degradation rate is reduced to 1% per 1000 hours. A power density of 1.5 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 600 to 750 degrees C operating range.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising scandia-stabilized zirconia, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 15 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising barium strontium cobalt ferrite disposed on the barrier layer.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a tin-rich surface region is described. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 2 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a tin substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours is 70% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF), wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the ionic conductivity of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.05 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium indium chloride ion-conductive solid with monoclinic structure and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. When z is 0.3, the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.3 V. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.2 to 0.45 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. After dehydration under vacuum at 200 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.47 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for preparing the same
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide solid electrolyte with an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more is described. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The composition forms a shell on the cathode particles that suppresses the space-charge layer, so that the halide serves as the coating layer. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.35 mS/cm or more.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by thermal evaporation. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The protective layer thickness is 120 nm to 600 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 97.8% or more. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.8% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 200 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The lithium battery is operated at 120 degrees C under a stack pressure of 200 kPa. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 100 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The dry electrode process with nitrile butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The additive content is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, the stack pressure is 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa, and the critical current density is 1 mA/cm2. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more, and wherein the content of the magnesium additive is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3InCl6. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6, wherein z is 0.1 to 0.35, and a method for producing the same are provided. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3InCl6. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.3 V. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The titanium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which erbium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO solid electrolyte in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. With hafnium substitution of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The oxide particles have a core of the perovskite-type LLTO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the sinterability of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.7 V or more.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. Specific examples are Li3YCl6. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The LLZO, Li3PS4, and LATP composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, LLTO, and Li2ZrO3 material. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries.
