Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in 1,2-dimethoxyethane at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 1 wt%. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and production method thereof
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. No solvent is used in the process, so the solid electrolyte does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers, a porosity of 5%, a tensile strength of 0.5 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 10 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state lithium battery. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 50 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 55% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 material. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 15 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. The lithium zirconate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of scandium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide ceramic ion conductor in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ScCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.2 to 0.45 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.2 to 0.45. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiF, Li3YCl6, and LiNbO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.7, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 420 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 600 MPa. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 600 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 80 degrees C after lamination. The module with 2 stacked cells has a voltage of 2 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 50 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 600 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6 and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 10 nm. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The lithium niobium tantalum oxide shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 4 nm to 20 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Amperometric ammonia sensor using an oxide ion conducting ceramic and gas sensor system
abstract: Disclosed is a mixed potential type sensor in which an oxide electrode and a gold electrode on a zirconia substrate generate a potential difference depending on the ammonia concentration. The sensing electrode comprises gold and a metal oxide and is printed on the ceramic and fired at 1000 degrees C. The auxiliary electrode of sodium nitrite makes the sensor selective to ammonia against interfering gases. The sensor output changes by 50 mV per decade of ammonia concentration in the range of 10 ppm to 1000 ppm. The electromotive force across the solid electrolyte follows the Nernst equation. The sensor element is sealed in a metal housing with a gas inlet protected by a double cover. The sensor detects ammonia with high selectivity and a response time of 5 seconds.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising sodium nitrite in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects ammonia.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 72:28 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.2 mS/cm. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12 and Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. When v is 0.5, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The LLTO, Li2ZrO3, and LATP composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.35 <= v <= 0.7, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 12 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid tin binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 70% or more are obtained. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a tin substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state battery using it. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The content of SiS2 is 3 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.8 mS/cm or more. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material. The solid electrolyte shows improved electrochemical window and cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ion-conductive solid particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. With a binder content of 2 wt% and a roll temperature of 80 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 30% or less. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.3 MPa or more, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid electrolytic capacitor having a porous aluminum anode body and a hybrid electrolyte
abstract: Provided is a multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor in which capacitor elements are stacked and connected in parallel. A re-formation step after polymer formation repairs defects in the dielectric film and reduces the leakage current. A capacitance of 220 microfarads is obtained in a case size of 7.3 mm by 4.3 mm. The dielectric oxide film is formed by anodizing the aluminum anode body in a phosphoric acid solution at a formation voltage of 2 to 4 times the rated voltage. The capacitor rated at 6.3 V can be used in a power supply circuit of an electronic device with a low ripple voltage. The capacitor shows improved heat resistance at 150 degrees C and can be mounted by reflow soldering.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising: anodizing a porous aluminum anode body to form a dielectric oxide film; impregnating the anode body with a dispersion of polypyrrole particles having a particle size of 20 nm to 100 nm; drying the dispersion to form a conductive polymer layer; and forming a carbon layer and a silver layer on the conductive polymer layer.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation and production method thereof
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 200 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 1 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% over 100 cycles. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.1 micrometers to 10 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 1200 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 125 cycles or more.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-SiS2 glass. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 1.3 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 24 hours, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 200 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. A lithium battery pack comprising 16 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 92% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The dopant gallium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1250 degrees C, and the resulting density is 92%. The Li2ZrO3 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 25 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 48 micrometers.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. A capacity retention of 92% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 77% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant gallium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The total ionic conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.35 <= v <= 0.7, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder and production method thereof
abstract: A solid electrolyte sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and a lithium secondary battery including the sheet are described. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 60 degrees C to form a continuous film. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. With a binder content of 1 wt% and a roll temperature of 60 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 10% or less. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the moisture stability and ionic conductivity of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.9 MPa or more, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 5 micrometers to 150 micrometers.

title: Lithium indium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 85% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 5 nm. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The lithium indium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ion-conductive solid particles are dispersed in heptane with a rubber binder and a dispersant. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the solid-state lithium battery. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 20 micrometers. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The Li3PS4 and LLZO material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 60 wt% to 80 wt%, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1.3 mS/cm or more.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 5 mol%. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The sintered body has a relative density of 92%, an average grain size of 10 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The LLZO, LLTO, and LATP composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.25 <= v <= 0.6, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 2 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte powder with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method of handling the same in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte powder has a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which 1 mol% to 5 mol% of the sulfur is substituted by oxygen, the oxygen being enriched in a surface region having a thickness of 2 nm to 20 nm. The powder is prepared by mechanically milling Li2S, P2S5, and Li2O in a dry room having a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower, heat-treating the milled mixture at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in argon, and exposing the heat-treated powder to an atmosphere having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hour to 3 hours so that the surface region is formed by controlled hydrolysis. The P-O bonds in the surface region are stable against water vapor, so that the cumulative hydrogen sulfide generation measured in a sealed 1 L chamber after 60 minutes of exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C is 5 cm3/g or less, and the ionic conductivity retention after the exposure is 85% or more. Because the surface region is thin and lithium-ion conductive, the grain boundary resistance of a pressed pellet remains 20% or less of the total resistance. The powder can be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box and is applicable to Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LLZO-containing composite electrolytes.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte powder comprising a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which 1 mol% to 5 mol% of sulfur is substituted by oxygen, wherein the oxygen is enriched in a surface region of the powder having a thickness of 2 nm to 20 nm, and wherein a cumulative hydrogen sulfide generation of the powder measured in a sealed chamber of 1 L after 60 minutes of exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C is 5 cm3/g or less.

title: Germanium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.5 V and lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.5 V. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state lithium battery. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The LATP and LLTO material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the sinterability is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 70% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 3.9 V or more.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of scandium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide solid electrolyte in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. After dehydration under vacuum at 300 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ScCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 5 wt% to 20 wt%.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region and lithium battery
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 2.3 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 75% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a silicon substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer comprises ion-conductive solid particles, a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% and a viscosity of 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 30 micrometers and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The wet film is dried at 60 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ion-conductive solid, and the layer shows improved interfacial resistance and sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 150 micrometers, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 200 mPa s to 10000 mPa s, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 15 wt% to 60 wt%.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering an aluminum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 93% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.05 to 0.4, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The sintered body has a relative density of 96%, an average grain size of 5 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 93% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 12 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 2 hours is 80% or more.

title: Solid oxide electrolysis cell and reversible fuel cell having a thin dense electrolyte
abstract: Described is an electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell with a 5 micrometer thick ceramic electrolyte. A power density of 1.5 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 500 to 650 degrees C operating range. The samarium-doped ceria solid electrolyte is co-sintered with the anode support at 1300 to 1400 degrees C. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 95%. Because the barrier layer prevents interfacial reaction with the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode, the degradation rate is reduced to 1% per 1000 hours. The reversible cell with a samarium-doped ceria electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. The glass sealant has a thermal expansion coefficient matched to the samarium-doped ceria electrolyte and seals the fuel and air compartments.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising samarium-doped ceria formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 95% or more.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using 1,2-dimethoxyethane
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt%. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state battery. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A solid-state battery comprising the LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The low electronic conductivity of the Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and LiF material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The oxidation stability limit is 4.3 V or more and the conductivity is 0.56 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The material comprises Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy for lithium battery
abstract: A Li6PS5X solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li3PS4 material. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein -0.05 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C.

title: Niobium-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A sintering aid comprising LiF is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The total ionic conductivity is 0.42 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 25 mol%.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 5 mS/cm. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li7P3S11 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiTaO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 15 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. In an embodiment the material is lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li3YCl6. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 35% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The material comprises Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, and wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.55, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ceramic ion conductor particles are dispersed in butyl butyrate with a rubber binder and a dispersant. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 30 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a lithium secondary battery. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved sheet formability and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 80 degrees C to 120 degrees C, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 40 wt% to 60 wt%, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 2 wt% to 10 wt%.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The solid electrolyte may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 330 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of scandium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium scandium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. In the orthorhombic structure, scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.3 to 0.55. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The titanium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium indium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium indium chloride formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. The Li2ZrO3, LiNbO3, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 60 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
