abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3PS4 and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). With the additive in an amount of 0.5 wt% and a stack pressure of 20 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.7%. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved cycle life and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 4 MPa to 100 MPa, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.2% or more.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 10 mol%. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1230 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm and a relative density of 94%. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the grain boundary resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 91% or more.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Negative electrode structure with a lithium fluoride and magnesium nucleation additive layer for suppressing dendrites in a solid-state lithium cell
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a solid-state lithium cell comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer comprising Li3PS4 or a garnet-type LLZO, and a nucleation additive layer disposed between them, the additive layer comprising lithium fluoride particles having an average size of 50 nm to 300 nm and magnesium particles in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 90:10 and having a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. During plating, lithium alloys with the magnesium to form uniformly distributed nucleation sites, while the lithium fluoride, which has an electronic conductivity below 1 x 10^-10 S/cm, blocks electron leakage into the ion-conductive solid and prevents the growth of lithium filaments along grain boundaries. During stripping, the alloy phase keeps the contact so that void formation at the interface is suppressed under a stack pressure of 2 MPa to 8 MPa. The structure raises the critical current density at 25 degrees C from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 2.5 mA/cm2 or more, lowers the interfacial resistance to 10 ohm cm2 or less, and keeps the ionic conductivity of the interface. A symmetric cell with the structure survives 500 plating and stripping cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 without short circuit with a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% or more.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a solid-state lithium cell, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and a nucleation additive layer disposed between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer, the nucleation additive layer comprising lithium fluoride particles having an average particle size of 50 nm to 300 nm and magnesium particles in a weight ratio of lithium fluoride to magnesium of 70:30 to 90:10, wherein the nucleation additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Moisture-tolerant lithium indium chloride solid electrolyte with a surface fluorination layer and method of recovering conductivity after humid exposure
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises particles of Li3InCl6 having a monoclinic crystal structure and a surface fluorination layer having a thickness of 2 nm to 15 nm in which 20% to 60% of the chloride at the surface is replaced by fluoride. The fluorination layer is formed by exposing the chloride powder to a gas mixture containing 1 vol% to 5 vol% of fluorine in argon at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C for 10 minutes to 60 minutes. Because the fluoride is far less hygroscopic than the chloride, the water uptake of the powder at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% or less, and the ionic conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 70% or more of the initial value of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Even when the powder absorbs water to form a hydrate, the conductivity is recovered to 90% or more by vacuum drying at 150 degrees C to 200 degrees C, so that the powder can be handled in a dry room and processed into a slurry. A positive electrode mixture containing the electrolyte, stable up to 4.3 V versus Li/Li+, together with a sulfide glass ceramic shows improved high-voltage stability and moisture stability in production.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte comprising particles of Li3InCl6 having a monoclinic crystal structure, wherein each particle has a surface fluorination layer having a thickness of 2 nm to 15 nm in which 20% to 60% of chloride at a surface of the particle is replaced by fluoride, and wherein a water uptake of the halide solid electrolyte at 25 degrees C and 10% relative humidity for 1 hour is 0.5 wt% or less.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a gallium-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 92% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1230 degrees C, and the resulting density is 95%. Specific examples are Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 92% or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 150 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C.

title: Lithium niobium tantalum oxide-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 15 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved interfacial resistance and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.5 nm to 75 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 65% or more.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of indium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ceramic ion conductor comprises a monoclinic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Br6. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.2 V versus Li/Li+. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li3YCl6. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 material. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. In the monoclinic structure, indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed bromide sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A precursor of the Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.47 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 solid electrolyte with reduced grain boundary resistance and lithium battery
abstract: A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12 and Al2O3 present at grain boundaries. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Sintering at 1250 degrees C with a lithium excess of 10 mol% gives a relative density of 95% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP and LLTO material. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The method gives reproducible densification and improved sinterability at a lower cost.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The Li3PS4 and LGPS material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 and LGPS material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.65, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and polytetrafluoroethylene are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. The module with 4 stacked cells has a voltage of 4 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate and the battery is a lithium battery with 4 stacked cells. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 300 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The separator layer is a sheet of 20 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more to the cell.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state lithium battery using it. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. A lithium excess of 5 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. An argyrodite phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The grain size is 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and the relative density is 92% or more after sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C. The LLZO, Li2ZrO3, and LATP material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the high-voltage stability of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 2 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein 0.05 <= v <= 0.4, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 92% or more.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Described is a lithium indium chloride solid electrolyte prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The oxidation stability limit is 4.1 V or more and the conductivity is 0.56 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. Suitable compositions include lithium fluoride (LiF). The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, InCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing LiI. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours.

title: Dendrite-suppressing magnesium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The additive content is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, the stack pressure is 10 MPa to 40 MPa, and the critical current density is 1 mA/cm2. The material comprises Li3YCl6 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the electronic conductivity of the ion-conductive solid layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The additive comprises magnesium in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li3YCl6 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The method prevents short circuit and improves the interfacial resistance and dendrite suppression without a thick protective layer.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more, and wherein the content of the magnesium additive is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the ionic conductivity of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein 1.3 <= a <= 1.7, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing SiS2. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 70:30, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by sputtering and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The Li3N layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ceramic ion conductor. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 200 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 1 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% over 100 cycles. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 80 nm to 400 nm.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The LLZO and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.1 <= x <= 0.55, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The binder is hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The solid content is 40 wt% to 60 wt%, the viscosity is 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers. An all-solid-state battery using the layer shows improved moisture stability and a thin electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.3 wt% to 15 wt%, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 25 wt% to 70 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less.

title: Dendrite-suppressing indium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which an indium-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. The additive comprises indium in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5% after 100 cycles. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li3YCl6. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the dendrite suppression. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression of the solid-state cell.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the indium additive is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 99% or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more.

title: Solid electrolyte slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer that has a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s. The binder is styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent anisole. The binder content is 3 wt%, the drying temperature is 60 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The LLZO and LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the solid electrolyte does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the solid electrolyte, and the layer shows improved ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 50 wt% to 70 wt%.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by cold isostatic pressing
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a stainless steel current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa through an elastic sheet. The structure with the stainless steel current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The cold isostatic pressing step at 600 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The bipolar stacking of 8 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a stainless steel current collector is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Dendrite-suppressing lithium fluoride additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and production method thereof
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. With the additive in an amount of 0.5 wt% and a stack pressure of 2 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99%. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%.

title: Lithium niobium tantalum oxide-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ceramic ion conductor layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The roll temperature is 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers after calendering. The LATP and Li7P3S11 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7P3S11. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 10% or less.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa with a zinc additive. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 4 mA/cm2. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The suppression of void formation improves the dendrite suppression and cycle life during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the content of the zinc additive is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium bromide ion-conductive solid prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, YBr3, and ZrBr4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiNbO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The material is also used as a coating layer on core particles of a nickel-rich positive electrode active material, with a coverage of 85% or more and a thickness of 5 nm to 20 nm. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 0.56 mS/cm or more. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 60 degrees C. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate forms a passivation film on the positive electrode that suppresses electrolyte oxidation at 4.3 V. The capacity retention of 88% after 1000 cycles is higher than that of an electrolyte without fluoroethylene carbonate. The cell charged to 4.3 V retains 88% of its capacity after 1000 cycles. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The combination of fluoroethylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The additive fluoroethylene carbonate decomposes on the negative electrode during the first charge and forms a passivation film rich in lithium fluoride.
first_claim: 1. An electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate, a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate, a first additive comprising fluoroethylene carbonate, and a second additive comprising a sulfur-containing compound, wherein a weight ratio of the first additive to the second additive is 1:0.2 to 1:2.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The coating layer has an average thickness of 5 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. The LiNbO3 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which lithium fluoride is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% to suppress dendrites. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), beta-Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6, and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more and a critical current density of 3 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The additive comprises lithium fluoride in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ceramic ion conductor layer onto an electrode of the solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the interfacial resistance and cycle life of the solid-state cell.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid oxygen binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an oxygen substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less. The solvent is a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state lithium battery. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: Provided is an electrolyte composition comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate at a concentration of 1.2 M and a film-forming additive. The electrolyte containing lithium tetrafluoroborate at 1.2 M is used in a lithium secondary battery charged to 4.4 V. The 1.2 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. A solid electrolyte interphase rich in inorganic components is formed on the graphite. The 1.2 M lithium tetrafluoroborate solution in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.4 V. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite is added in an amount of 2 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The additive tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite reduces gas generation during storage at 45 degrees C and improves safety.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium tetrafluoroborate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate; and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 2 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which lithium fluoride is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% to suppress dendrites. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 3 mA/cm2. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the lithium secondary battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The ion-conductive solid may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved high-voltage stability and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 0.5 wt% to 25 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 4 MPa to 100 MPa.

title: Lithium phosphorus oxynitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The inorganic layer is formed by sputtering to a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved ionic conductivity and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.8% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more.

title: Positive electrode for a lithium-sulfur battery with a high sulfur loading and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Described is a lithium sulfide cathode that is activated by a first charge above 3.5 V. With a sulfur loading of 2 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. A lithium-sulfur pouch cell comprising the composite cathode and retaining 90% of its capacity after 500 cycles is also described. The carbon coating on the iron sulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using carboxymethyl cellulose. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 90%. A separator coated with graphene traps the polysulfides on the cathode side.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising graphene; iron sulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and production method thereof
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 80% or more. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The ion-conductive solid may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the solid-state battery. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 80% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. An H2S generation of 4 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 2 cm3/g. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 80% or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobium tantalum oxide formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The Li3InCl6 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The Li3InCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more.

title: Gallium-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 92% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The disclosure is applicable to lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1230 degrees C, and the resulting density is 92%. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The resulting Li2ZrO3 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers, and wherein 0.1 <= v <= 0.45, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state lithium battery using it. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LGPS material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LGPS composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. Suitable compositions include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of P2O5 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-GeS2 glass. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase.
