The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. After heat treatment at 320 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 3.1 mS/cm. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the content of LiI is 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP and LLTO material. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 10% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 190 degrees C to 380 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 24 hours.

title: Slurry composition for an ion-conductive solid layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which ion-conductive solid particles are dispersed in xylene with a rubber binder and a dispersant. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state lithium battery. The slurry has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO and LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 30 micrometers. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 16 stacked cells
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 20 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by uniaxial pressing and the release film is peeled. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 100 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 16 stacked cells. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 20 micrometer separator layer. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 100 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The separator layer is a solid electrolyte layer of 20 micrometers comprising sulfide particles bonded by styrene-butadiene rubber.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and LGPS material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 8.5 mS/cm. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 6.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.4 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-GeS2 glass. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A precursor of the Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 72:28 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 8 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LGPS material. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a lithium fluoride-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. The Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The cell shows no short circuit for 500 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 5 MPa. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The additive comprises lithium fluoride in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The additive suppresses lithium dendrites and improves the interfacial resistance of the solid-state cell.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.8% or more.

title: Dendrite-suppressing silver additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa with a silver additive. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.3% after 100 cycles. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. A stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The additive comprises silver in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 5.2 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LATP and LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A capacity retention of 80% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The oxide ion-conductive solid enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 25 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 65% or more.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: Provided is a phosphate-based NASICON ion-conductive solid in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. The LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The oxide particles have a core of the phosphate-based NASICON phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A capacity retention of 88% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the ionic conductivity and sinterability of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 83% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in tetrahydrofuran at 80 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The solvent is tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the moisture stability of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. The Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. When fired at 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the moisture stability of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, and wherein 0.35 <= y/a <= 0.65.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the electronic conductivity of the solid electrolyte layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The cell shows no short circuit for 300 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 10 MPa. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved ionic conductivity and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa, and wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. A precursor of the Li2ZrO3 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 material. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based solid-state lithium battery is described. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Nickel accounts for 70 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer that has a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s. The binder is styrene-butadiene rubber in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent heptane. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The binder content is 5 wt%, the drying temperature is 100 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 50 wt% to 70 wt%.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 8 mol%. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1250 degrees C, and the resulting density is 96%. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The method gives reproducible densification and improved ionic conductivity at a lower cost.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1050 degrees C to 1400 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 1 micrometers to 60 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 88% or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor and to a lithium battery including the same. A solid-state battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The sintered body has a relative density of 97%, an average grain size of 10 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein 0.35 <= v <= 0.7, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 7 mol% to 15 mol%.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The solvent is a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt%. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and Li6PS5Cl material. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Hafnium-substituted lithium scandium bromide solid electrolyte with trigonal structure and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a trigonal halide solid electrolyte in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 3 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The material comprises Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 60 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 3 wt% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 0.9 mS/cm or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2WO4 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 10 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Gallium-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a gallium-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 93% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. The sintered body has a relative density of 96%, an average grain size of 10 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the sinterability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.15 <= v <= 0.5, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 3 nm. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The high coverage of the coating results in improved ionic conductivity at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl and LGPS material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which zinc is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% to suppress dendrites. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The zinc additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. A precursor of the LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The critical current density is 2.8 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved interfacial resistance and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the content of the zinc additive is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in ethyl acetate to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. A solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 1 wt%. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the ionic conductivity of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 15 mol%. The total ionic conductivity is 0.56 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The dopant niobium occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.25 to 0.6, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 92% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed bromine-iodine substitution. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li3PS4 and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein 1 <= a <= 1.8, and wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.65.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 4 mS/cm. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of SiS2 is 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 210 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 70 mol% or more of the transition metals. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The coating layer has an average thickness of 15 nm and a coverage of 90%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.5 nm to 75 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C.

title: Solid electrolytic capacitor with a conductive polymer solid electrolyte layer and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Described is a solid electrolytic capacitor element whose leakage current is reduced by a repair step of the dielectric film. The conductive polymer layer is formed by chemical polymerization of the monomer in the presence of an oxidant followed by impregnation with a polymer dispersion. A capacitance of 470 microfarads is obtained in a case size of 7.3 mm by 4.3 mm. The hybrid structure improves the self-healing of the dielectric film on the tantalum anode. A solid electrolyte of poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) replaces the liquid electrolyte of a conventional electrolytic capacitor. The conductive polymer layer contains a polyhydric alcohol as an additive that improves the coverage on the dielectric. The capacitor shows improved heat resistance at 125 degrees C and can be mounted by reflow soldering.
first_claim: 1. A conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) particles doped with polystyrene sulfonate, a polyhydric alcohol, and water, wherein the particles have a median diameter of 20 nm to 100 nm.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2ZrO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The LiNbO3 and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiNbO3 and Li2ZrO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Amperometric ammonia sensor using an oxide ion conducting ceramic and gas sensor system
abstract: An electrochemical gas sensor for detecting ammonia comprises a sodium beta-alumina ceramic, a sensing electrode comprising platinum, and a reference electrode exposed to a reference gas. The built-in heater shortens the warm-up time of the sensor to 500 degrees C. The protective layer improves the durability of the sodium beta-alumina sensor in an exhaust gas. The sensing electrode comprises platinum and a metal oxide and is printed on the ceramic and fired at 1000 degrees C. The ceramic is sodium beta-alumina and conducts ions at the operating temperature of 500 degrees C. The sensor output changes by 50 mV per decade of ammonia concentration in the range of 10 ppm to 1000 ppm.
first_claim: 1. A potentiometric gas sensor comprising an ion conducting ceramic, a sensing electrode, a reference electrode, and an auxiliary electrode comprising sodium carbonate in contact with the sensing electrode and the ceramic, wherein the sensor detects ammonia.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in ethyl propionate to give a sulfide ceramic ion conductor precursor. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm or more. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less.

title: Electrolyte composition comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate and a film-forming additive
abstract: A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate dissolved in ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate and lithium bis(oxalato)borate as an additive in an amount of 2 wt%. The cell retains 85% of its capacity after 300 cycles at 25 degrees C and shows a thickness increase of 5% or less after storage at 45 degrees C for 4 weeks. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.4 V. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.4 V. A pouch type lithium ion battery comprising a nickel-rich positive electrode, a graphite negative electrode, and the electrolyte is also provided. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and ethyl methyl carbonate; and lithium bis(oxalato)borate in an amount of 2 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium zirconate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm is provided. The LiNbO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and cycle life and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The average thickness of the coating is 6 nm to 30 nm, the coverage is 80% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more.

title: Planar solid oxide fuel cell stack with metal interconnects and a glass sealant
abstract: Described is an electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell with a 10 micrometer thick ceramic electrolyte. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte and the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate. The gadolinium-doped ceria electrolyte of 98% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. The cell operates at 500 to 650 degrees C with a power density of 1.2 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 100 cycles. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 98%. Because the barrier layer prevents interfacial reaction with the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode, the degradation rate is reduced to 1% per 1000 hours.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising gadolinium-doped ceria and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 500 to 650 degrees C.

title: Dendrite-suppressing indium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the solid electrolyte. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material comprises Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4, and the electronic conductivity of the solid electrolyte layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1.5 mA/cm2. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 4 MPa to 100 MPa.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO ion-conductive solid in which germanium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 50 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 2 mol% to 40 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using acetonitrile for lithium battery
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The LLZO and LATP material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.9 wt% or less, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 32 wt%.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting solid electrolyte film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. No solvent is used in the process, so the solid electrolyte does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LATP and Li3PS4 material. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the cycle life of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.6 MPa or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.05 wt% to 2.5 wt%.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 4 mS/cm. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte shows improved cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using acetonitrile and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. In a solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 5 mS/cm. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The solvent is acetonitrile, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a ceramic ion conductor with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less.
