abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li3YCl6, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LiF, LLZO, and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the lithium secondary battery. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li3YCl6. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.1 mS/cm or more.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to a solid-state battery comprising the same. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Firing is performed at 480 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein 1.2 <= a <= 1.6.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.1 to 0.45, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1150 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm and a relative density of 95%. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 950 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 25 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 87% or more.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by solution casting followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 200 nm. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ceramic ion conductor at the negative electrode is suppressed and the dendrite suppression is improved.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.8% or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 10 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite solid electrolyte having anion disorder for lithium battery
abstract: A solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and iodine. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The ion-conductive component may be Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LGPS and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 11.2 mS/cm. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state lithium battery. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein 1.4 <= a <= 1.8, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film without any solvent. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers, a porosity of 10%, a tensile strength of 3 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 100 degrees C to form a continuous film. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with niobium and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. The LLZO material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 94% or more, and wherein 0.25 <= v <= 0.6, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and method for producing the same
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 and LGPS material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The content of SiS2 is 5 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.8 mS/cm or more. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of SiS2 is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO solid electrolyte in which zirconium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 88%. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 100 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 73% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid arsenic-free antimony binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity retention is 90%. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more.

title: In situ polymerized electrolyte for a lithium ion battery and method of manufacturing the battery
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. A lithium secondary battery comprising the polymer electrolyte, a positive electrode, and a lithium metal or graphite negative electrode is also provided. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 40 degrees C. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 40 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The semi-interpenetrating network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 1.0 mS/cm. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 40 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a semi-interpenetrating network of polycarbonate and lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 30 micrometers or less.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt% or less. The ion-conductive solid may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 120 degrees C to 300 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 8 mol%. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1230 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm and a relative density of 97%. Suitable compositions include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol%, and wherein 0.05 <= v <= 0.4, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 94% or more.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form an ion-conductive solid of high conductivity. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiF and Li3InCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is beta-Li3PS4, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the lithium secondary battery. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 80%. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The hafnium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the sinterability and high-voltage stability in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer comprises ion-conductive solid particles, a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The binder is styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent anisole. The binder content is 3 wt%, the drying temperature is 120 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the ionic conductivity of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 40 wt% to 60 wt%, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing SiS2. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide ion-conductive solid and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 3.1 mS/cm. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 16 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 170 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 100%.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3BO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The Li3InCl6, Li2ZrO3, and LiNbO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The material comprises Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 70% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by roll pressing at 100 MPa and 120 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 100 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The edge of the 50 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The lithium battery is operated at 120 degrees C under a stack pressure of 100 kPa. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: An argyrodite-type solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and LGPS material. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.15 <= x <= 0.95, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder for lithium battery
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers, a porosity of 10%, a tensile strength of 3 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. An all-solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved interfacial resistance and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a thio-LISICON phase and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the electrochemical window of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 170 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell with a barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode and a diffusion barrier layer of doped ceria
abstract: Described is an electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell with a 10 micrometer thick ceramic electrolyte. The anode support contains nickel oxide and samarium-doped ceria in a weight ratio of 60:40 and has a porosity of 30% to 40% after reduction. The electrolyte layer has a thickness of 10 micrometers and a relative density of 98%, and the open circuit voltage is 1.1 V at 500 to 650 degrees C. Hydrogen or reformed natural gas is supplied to the anode and air is supplied to the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode at 500 to 650 degrees C. The reversible cell with a samarium-doped ceria electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. The stack shows stable operation over 100 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 500 to 650 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising samarium-doped ceria formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 98% or more.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO solid electrolyte in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. A capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved sinterability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 80% or more.

title: Surface mount solid electrolytic capacitor and method of reducing leakage current
abstract: A hybrid capacitor combining a conductive polymer layer and an electrolytic solution is described. A carbon layer and a silver paste layer are formed on the polypyrrole layer to serve as the cathode lead-out. The niobium capacitor element is encapsulated in an epoxy resin with the anode lead and cathode terminal exposed. The dispersion of polypyrrole gives a uniform polymer layer and a high capacitance appearance rate for the 47 microfarad rating. The polypyrrole layer lowers the equivalent series resistance to 15 milliohms compared with manganese dioxide. The equivalent series resistance is 15 milliohms or less and the leakage current is 0.01 CV or less. A solid electrolyte of polypyrrole replaces the liquid electrolyte of a conventional electrolytic capacitor.
first_claim: 1. A conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor, comprising polypyrrole particles doped with naphthalenesulfonate, a polyhydric alcohol, and water, wherein the particles have a median diameter of 20 nm to 100 nm.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ceramic ion conductor film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The tensile strength is 0.3 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers, and wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which lithium fluoride is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% to suppress dendrites. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The cell shows no short circuit for 1000 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 20 MPa. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4, and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 500 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved electrochemical window and cycle life compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less, and wherein -0.05 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.2 V. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The median particle diameter D50 is 1 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The LiF and Li3YCl6 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ion-conductive component may be lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the moisture stability at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 470 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO solid electrolyte in which zirconium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.5 V. Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the grain boundary resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 3.9 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 2 mol% to 40 mol%.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into a solid electrolyte layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The LiF layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The Li3PS4 and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% after 100 cycles. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved cycle life and dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.8% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 120 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of scandium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ceramic ion conductor comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.1 to 0.35. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ScCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The zirconium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 1.8 mS/cm. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A capacity retention of 80% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4, and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Hafnium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ion-conductive solid stable above 4.8 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by hafnium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.8 V. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the sinterability of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 100 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ceramic ion conductor containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 60% to 95%.

title: Method for co-sintering an anode support and a dense zirconia electrolyte layer for a solid oxide fuel cell
abstract: Described is an electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell with a 15 micrometer thick ceramic electrolyte. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 500 to 650 degrees C. The lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode gives a low polarization resistance at 500 to 650 degrees C. The solid electrolyte layer of lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite conducts oxide ions and separates the fuel from the air. The cell operates at 500 to 650 degrees C with a power density of 0.8 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 100 cycles. Because the barrier layer prevents interfacial reaction with the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode, the degradation rate is reduced to 1% per 1000 hours. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte and the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate.
first_claim: 1. A tubular solid oxide fuel cell comprising a nickel cermet anode tube, an electrolyte layer comprising lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite formed on the anode tube, and a cathode layer, wherein the electrolyte layer has a relative density of 98% or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 10 cm3/g or less. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The ion-conductive solid may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 1 hours is 65% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 25 cm3/g or less.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, which gives an oxidation limit of 4.2 V or more and a conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm or more. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.2 V or more.

title: Lithium indium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The resulting Li3InCl6 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which an indium-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The material comprises Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the electronic conductivity of the solid electrolyte layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.5% after 100 cycles. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. A stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 25 MPa, and wherein the content of the indium additive is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The content of Li2O is 5 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 60% to 95%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The LGPS, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the cycle life of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from acetonitrile, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a ceramic ion conductor with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 5 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tantalum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. When v is 0.5, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Sintering is performed at 1150 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved cycle life and interfacial resistance compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 92% or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
