abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a tin-rich surface region is described. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The tin substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 550 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.1 mS/cm or more. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the grain boundary resistance are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a tin substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein 0.4 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 500 kPa
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 120 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The lithium battery is operated at 120 degrees C under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ion-conductive solid using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 5 mol%. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A lithium secondary battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The total ionic conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. A lithium excess of 5 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 2 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 94% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1150 degrees C to 1300 degrees C.

title: SiS2-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. After heat treatment at 260 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 4 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of SiS2 is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-butadiene rubber
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer. The binder is styrene-butadiene rubber in an amount of 2 wt% to 10 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 30 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The slurry has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 250 mPa s to 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The LLZO and LATP material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the layer shows improved ionic conductivity and a thin electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 40 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 15 wt% to 60 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 150 micrometers.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 4 mS/cm. The LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ceramic ion conductor. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. With the additive in an amount of 2 wt% and a stack pressure of 2 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99%. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved interfacial resistance and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 60 cycles or more, and wherein the content of the zinc additive is 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Tin-substituted titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ceramic ion conductor stable above 5.2 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more is described. The positive electrode active material is a 5 V spinel, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The oxidation potential is 5.2 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 2 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The widened electrochemical window improves the sinterability and ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 83% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.045 or less. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein -0.05 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7P3S11. The material comprises Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 40 hours, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C.

title: Method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a ceramic ion conductor film without any solvent. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. A sheet of 80 micrometers has an areal resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less at 25 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery using the sheet shows improved cycle life and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 10% or less, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers, and wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in acetonitrile to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using tetrahydrofuran and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A precursor of the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 80 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 4 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The structure with the copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The warm isostatic pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a copper current collector is also provided. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa through an elastic sheet.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium iron phosphate on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 20 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by warm isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. The arsenic-free antimony content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 20 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1 mS/cm or more. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in 1,2-dimethoxyethane at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt%. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved moisture stability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a thio-LISICON phase for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The LGPS and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Crystallization is performed at 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the content of LiI is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Br6 and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium bromide ceramic ion conductor prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. An all-solid-state lithium battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. The LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.5 V versus Li/Li+. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved electrochemical window and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more.

title: Lithium borate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm is provided. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The Li3InCl6 and Li2ZrO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.8 nm to 40 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 30 mol% or more.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tantalum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 91% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. Sintering is performed at 1200 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The grain size is 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and the relative density is 91% or more after sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 86% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 3 mol% to 23 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.24 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for forming a conductive polymer layer on a dielectric oxide of a solid electrolytic capacitor
abstract: Described is a solid electrolytic capacitor element whose leakage current is reduced by a repair step of the dielectric film. The capacitor rated at 16 V can be used in a power supply circuit of an electronic device with a low ripple voltage. The conductive polymer layer contains a polyhydric alcohol as an additive that improves the coverage on the dielectric. A capacitance of 47 microfarads is obtained in a case size of 7.3 mm by 4.3 mm. The polypyrrole is doped with polystyrene sulfonate and has a particle size of 20 nm to 100 nm in the dispersion. The polystyrene sulfonate doped polymer keeps its conductivity after 125 degrees C storage. The solid electrolyte layer covers the dielectric oxide film inside the pores of the anode body.
first_claim: 1. A solid electrolytic capacitor comprising: an anode body comprising a porous sintered body of aluminum; a dielectric layer formed on a surface of the anode body; a conductive polymer layer disposed on the dielectric layer and comprising polypyrrole doped with polystyrene sulfonate; and a cathode layer comprising carbon and silver disposed on the conductive polymer layer, wherein an equivalent series resistance of the capacitor at 100 kHz is 8 milliohms or less.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using ethyl propionate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in ethyl propionate to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the solid-state lithium battery. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm. A solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant aluminum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 92% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C, and wherein 0.25 <= v <= 0.6.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-LiI glass. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 40 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the content of LiI is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide ceramic ion conductor in which tin substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.3 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.7 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: titanium disulfide positive electrode material with a carbon coating and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a transition metal sulfide active material that intercalates lithium with a high capacity. In an embodiment the cathode is pressed against a sulfide solid electrolyte layer instead of a separator. The graphene framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of titanium disulfide. The cathode with a loading of 3 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The capacity retention after 100 cycles is 90% at 25 degrees C. The initial capacity of 1400 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode contains the composite and carboxymethyl cellulose. Polysulfide dissolution from the titanium disulfide cathode into the electrolyte is suppressed by a polar metal oxide additive that adsorbs polysulfides.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode for a lithium secondary battery, comprising a current collector and a positive electrode mixture layer disposed thereon, the positive electrode mixture layer comprising titanium disulfide, graphene, and carboxymethyl cellulose, wherein a loading of the titanium disulfide is 3 mg/cm2 or more.

title: Self-supporting ceramic ion conductor sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The tensile strength is 1.8 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The method shortens the process and improves the cycle life of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.8 MPa or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 24 hours is 75% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a silicon substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in ethyl propionate at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a thio-LISICON phase for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li6PS5Cl material. The content of LiI is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.8 mS/cm or more. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%, and wherein the content of LiI is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours.

title: Solid electrolyte slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer comprises solid electrolyte particles, a polyisobutylene binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C in an oven. A halide coating layer may be used together with the solid electrolyte to improve the cycle life of the lithium secondary battery. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 15 micrometers. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the sheet formability of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a silicon-rich surface region is described. The silicon substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the solid-state lithium battery. An H2S generation of 4 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 2 cm3/g. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a silicon substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 75% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less.

title: Tin-substituted NASICON-type LATP ion-conductive solid stable above 5 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an ion-conductive solid whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The oxide particles have a core of the NASICON-type LATP phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in tin. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.7 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.35 mS/cm or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The suspension has a solid concentration of 4 wt% to 16 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The material comprises Li7P3S11, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C.

title: Lithium tantalate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 75% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 30% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 15% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 60% or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a thio-LISICON phase for lithium battery
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. After heat treatment at 280 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved moisture stability and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of P2O5 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. Specific examples are lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The LiNbO3 and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The solid electrolyte may comprise beta-Li3PS4. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The silicon substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. After exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours, the conductivity retention is 70%. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a silicon substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.4 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 7.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.12 or less. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 6.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, and wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.65.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers, a porosity of 5%, a tensile strength of 1 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. A solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.09 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C, and wherein 1.1 <= a <= 1.9.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The material comprises Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 80% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the moisture stability and sinterability.
first_claim: 1.
