A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. After heat treatment at 280 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.2 mS/cm. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the moisture stability of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 190 degrees C to 380 degrees C, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 0.6 mol% to 12 mol%.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor stable against oxidation above 5.2 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The positive electrode active material is a 5 V spinel, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. With zirconium substitution of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The widened electrochemical window improves the grain boundary resistance of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.9 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 87% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.21 mS/cm or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12 and LiF present at grain boundaries. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. Specific examples are Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.28 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the solid electrolyte. The additive content is 2 wt% to 10 wt%, the stack pressure is 5 MPa to 20 MPa, and the critical current density is 3 mA/cm2. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3YCl6, and the electronic conductivity of the solid electrolyte layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. A solid-state lithium cell using the structure shows improved ionic conductivity and operates at a lower stack pressure.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.2% or more, and wherein the content of the magnesium additive is 0.5 wt% to 25 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.2 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, YBr3, and HfBr4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. A precursor of the LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. When z is 0.3, the conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.3 V. The LiF, Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the ionic conductivity at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45.

title: Argyrodite solid electrolyte with a lithium-rich surface composition matched to niobate-coated positive electrode active materials
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for use in a positive electrode mixture together with a coated positive electrode active material has an argyrodite crystal structure and a bulk composition represented by Li6PS5Cl, and a surface region having a thickness of 3 nm to 20 nm in which the lithium to phosphorus atomic ratio is 7.0 to 8.5, higher than the bulk ratio of 6.0, as determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The surface region, formed by treating the fired powder with lithium ethoxide in ethanol and drying at 150 degrees C to 200 degrees C, matches the lithium chemical potential of a lithium niobate coating layer on the active material so that lithium depletion at the coating interface and the resulting space-charge layer are suppressed. The solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C, and a positive electrode mixture containing the solid electrolyte and niobate-coated LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 shows an interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V of 25 ohm cm2 or less, 40% lower than that of an untreated argyrodite. The surface region also lowers the hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air by 30% or more, and an all-solid-state battery using the mixture shows improved cycle life; Li10GeP2S12 type conductors can be treated in the same way.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte comprising a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure and a bulk composition represented by Li6PS5Cl, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a surface region having a thickness of 3 nm to 20 nm in which a lithium to phosphorus atomic ratio determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 7.0 to 8.5, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 95% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The Li2ZrO3 and LLTO material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. When v is 0.25, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 87% or more, and wherein 0.06 <= v <= 0.75, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 1 micrometers to 60 micrometers.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2WO4 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li3InCl6. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) and has an average thickness of 4 nm to 20 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and nickel content of 70 mol% or more. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 65% or more.

title: Zirconium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ion-conductive solid stable above 5.2 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO ion-conductive solid in which zirconium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 83% or more. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LATP and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 83% or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.65.

title: Tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a nickel cermet anode and a samarium-doped ceria electrolyte
abstract: A method for manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell by tape casting a samarium-doped ceria electrolyte green sheet and laminating it on an anode support green body is provided. A power density of 0.8 W/cm2 at 0.7 V is obtained at the upper end of the 650 to 800 degrees C operating range. The cathode comprises barium strontium cobalt ferrite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified. The reversible cell with a samarium-doped ceria electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. Hydrogen or reformed natural gas is supplied to the anode and air is supplied to the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode at 650 to 800 degrees C. The barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode gives a low polarization resistance at 650 to 800 degrees C.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising samarium-doped ceria and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 650 to 800 degrees C.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor that remains stable up to 5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state lithium battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the grain boundary resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.21 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.7 V or more.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid tin binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The resulting Li7P3S11 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a tin substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Slurry composition for a solid electrolyte layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer
abstract: Provided is a slurry in which solid electrolyte particles are dispersed in xylene with a rubber binder and a dispersant. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C in an oven. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The powder used for the sheet is prepared by a wet-chemical synthesis with filtration and drying, and the moisture exposure is controlled by a dew point of -40 degrees C. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% and a viscosity of 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 20 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid that remains stable up to 4.8 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.8 V. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The oxide ion-conductive solid enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 80% or more.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Li3N layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by atomic layer deposition. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 500 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99% over 100 cycles. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The bilayer structure improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life compared with a single inorganic layer.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 50 nm to 3000 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 50 cycles or more.

title: Zirconium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.8 V and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a ceramic ion conductor whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.8 V. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the solid-state battery. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The positive electrode active material is a 5 V spinel, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the sinterability is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 4 cm3/g or less. The oxygen substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 2 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an oxygen substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm and a retention of 85% after humid exposure. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. The material comprises Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a silicon substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and production method thereof
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid and to a lithium battery including the same. A sintering aid comprising LiF is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. A lithium excess of 5 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The method gives reproducible densification and improved grain boundary resistance at a lower cost.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.05 <= v <= 0.4, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 2 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 91% or more.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A wet film of an ion-conductive solid cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The binder is styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent xylene. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The viscosity of 1000 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which zirconium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. The material is also used as a coating layer on core particles of a nickel-rich positive electrode active material, with a coverage of 85% or more and a thickness of 5 nm to 20 nm. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A precursor of the LiF, Li3YCl6, and Li2ZrO3 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The LiF, Li3YCl6, and Li2ZrO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 1.47 mS/cm or more. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.5, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 3.7 V or more.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid comprising a crystal phase of the Li6PS5X type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both bromine and iodine. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ion-conductive solid exhibits an ionic conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The ion-conductive solid provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen Li6PS5X of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 680 degrees C, and wherein 0.9 <= a <= 1.7.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobium tantalum oxide and to a method for producing the same. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 8 nm. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The lithium niobium tantalum oxide shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1. The polyacrylonitrile electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 40 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polyacrylonitrile based electrolyte of 50 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, and a polymer electrolyte disposed therebetween, wherein the polymer electrolyte comprises a thermally crosslinked network of polyacrylonitrile and lithium perchlorate, and wherein the polymer electrolyte has a thickness of 50 micrometers or less.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and polyisobutylene
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a ceramic ion conductor is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 30 micrometers. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the dispersant is an amine-based dispersant in an amount of 0.1 wt% to 1 wt%. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ceramic ion conductor does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ceramic ion conductor, and the layer shows improved cycle life and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 70%. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of SiS2 is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The LGPS, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours, and wherein the content of LiI is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C.

assignee_std: CORAST INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tantalum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 93% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1250 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm and a relative density of 96%. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the sinterability of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.42 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 12 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid that remains stable up to 5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the ionic conductivity of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 85% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 5 mol%. A solid-state battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1150 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm and a relative density of 92%. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.11 <= v <= 0.8, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 950 degrees C to 1300 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 0 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and titanium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.2 V. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6. After dehydration under vacuum at 350 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6 material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, YCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The titanium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the high-voltage stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa with a lithium fluoride additive. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The cell shows no short circuit for 1000 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 2 MPa. The disclosure is applicable to lithium fluoride (LiF), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the electronic conductivity of the ion-conductive solid layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa, and wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Lithium niobium tantalum oxide-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobium tantalum oxide and to a method for producing the same. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium fluoride (LiF). The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 3.1 mS/cm. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the content of GeS2 is 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in acetonitrile at 40 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO material. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The reaction at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 300 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. The Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 60% to 95%, and wherein the content of GeS2 is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobate and to a method for producing the same. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The solid electrolyte is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 30% or more.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LiF, Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6 material. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6. No solvent is used in the process, so the solid electrolyte does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The tensile strength is 0.6 MPa or more and the elongation at break is 5% or more. The method shortens the process and improves the electrochemical window of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 30% or less, and wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.6 MPa or more.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer that has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 15 micrometers. The slurry has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LiF and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved ionic conductivity and dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 75 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.3 wt% to 15 wt%.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a solid electrolyte film without any solvent. With a binder content of 2 wt% and a roll temperature of 100 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 30% or less. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 100 degrees C to form a continuous film. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. No solvent is used in the process, so the solid electrolyte does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LATP and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The method shortens the process and improves the interfacial resistance of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.2 MPa or more.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The silver additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. With the additive in an amount of 5 wt% and a stack pressure of 2 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.7%. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and Li3YCl6. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more, and wherein the content of the silver additive is 2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a silicon-rich surface region is described. A solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The silicon substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 80% or more.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. In a solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The tin substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 24 hours is 65% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a tin substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium battery
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved grain boundary resistance and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of LiI is 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tantalate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tantalate and to a method for producing the same. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ion-conductive component may be lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3YCl6. The coating layer has an average thickness of 10 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 60% relative to uncoated particles. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous.
