title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A Li6PS5X phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The oxidation potential is 4.5 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Part of the titanium in the phosphate-based NASICON phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 3.9 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 50 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by solution casting followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The protective layer thickness is 200 nm to 1000 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 97.8% or more. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 500 nm. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.05 micrometers to 5 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 96.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 50 nm to 3000 nm.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet having a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and a porosity of 10% or less is provided. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. With a binder content of 3 wt% and a roll temperature of 80 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 10% or less. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LATP and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the interfacial resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.3 wt% to 15 wt%, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 160 degrees C.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of an ion-conductive solid with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 1.2 MPa or more. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. With a binder content of 2 wt% and a roll temperature of 100 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 30% or less. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The disclosure is applicable to Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the cycle life of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers, and wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 30% or less.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the Li6PS5X family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.045 or less. Firing is performed at 520 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.65, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The oxygen substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.1 mS/cm or more. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. The Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an oxygen substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in ethyl acetate to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved sinterability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the residual solvent content is 0.3 wt% or less, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The LiNbO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid provides improved moisture stability compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less, and wherein -0.05 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant gallium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The sintered body has a relative density of 97%, an average grain size of 2 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved high-voltage stability and sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.42 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol%.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. An H2S generation of 4 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved moisture stability and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Tungsten-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density for lithium battery
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12 and Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The LATP material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using acetonitrile and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less. The Li7P3S11 and LLZO material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.9 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7P3S11. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using nitrile butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 200 MPa and 120 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The cold isostatic pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. A lithium battery pack comprising 16 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 200 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Ceramic ion conductor slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer comprises ceramic ion conductor particles, a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The binder content is 2 wt%, the drying temperature is 80 degrees C, and the decrease in conductivity after slurry processing is 20% or less. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and beta-Li3PS4. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the ceramic ion conductor does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the sheet formability of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising butyl butyrate in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the solid content of the slurry is 40 wt% to 60 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The arsenic-free antimony content of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 1.6 mS/cm or more. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl and LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours is 75% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for producing the same
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 5.2 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 85% or more. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The oxide particles have a core of the phosphate-based NASICON phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in zirconium. The widened electrochemical window improves the high-voltage stability of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 85% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by roll pressing
abstract: Described is a dry electrode process in which an active material, a conductive agent, and polytetrafluoroethylene are mixed without a solvent and formed into a film. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 16 cells and a case is also provided. The laminate of 16 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 120 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 100 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 120 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a solid electrolyte with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 40 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 100 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 72:28 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 4 mS/cm. The P2O5 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 30% to 65%, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium borate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium borate and to a method for producing the same. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 15 nm. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiNbO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and cycle life and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet having a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and a porosity of 20% or less is provided. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. The LATP and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The LATP and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.6 MPa or more, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an ion-conductive solid whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. A capacity retention of 88% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The material comprises Li7P3S11, and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 100 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 73% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less, and wherein -0.05 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the lithium secondary battery. The silicon substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours is 75% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a silicon substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li2ZrO3 and LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The inorganic layer is formed by atomic layer deposition to a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 150 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved sinterability and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 200 nm to 1000 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. A precursor of the Li3PS4 and LGPS material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The ion-conductive solid shows improved cycle life and electrochemical window compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the content of P2O5 is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ion-conductive solid with reduced grain boundary resistance and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with tungsten and sintered with LiF is described. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. When v is 0.2, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.4 mS/cm. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.05 <= v <= 0.4, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state battery. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The LLZO and LATP material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coating layer has an average thickness of 3 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The lithium zirconate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the sheet formability and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and lithium battery
abstract: A Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The raw materials of the ceramic ion conductor are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.045 or less. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm. The Li7P3S11 and LGPS composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein 0.4 <= x <= 0.85, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) disposed on the surface of the core particles. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3InCl6 and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 50% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours is 80% or more.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: An ion-conductive solid sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and a solid-state lithium battery including the sheet are described. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The sheet has a thickness of 20 micrometers, a porosity of 5%, a tensile strength of 1 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The method shortens the process and improves the interfacial resistance of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.6 MPa or more, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 10% or less, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 80:20 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li7P3S11 material. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li7P3S11. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 8 hours, and wherein the content of LiI is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the solid-state lithium battery. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 5 mS/cm. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The suspension concentration is 10 wt%, the reaction temperature is 40 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 200 degrees C. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 5 wt% to 20 wt%.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium indium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction for lithium battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The composition further comprises a lithium metal halide in which the chloride anion sublattice is close-packed, and the halide is synthesized together with the main phase. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3InCl6. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. The Li2ZrO3 and Li3InCl6 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of scandium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide solid electrolyte of scandium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.5 V. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. In the orthorhombic structure, scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 3 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved moisture stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. The Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the sinterability of the product.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. A halogen-rich Li6PS5X with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 4 mS/cm. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The material comprises Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and production method thereof
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 96% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The total ionic conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved grain boundary resistance compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The oxide particles have a core of the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. Suitable compositions include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid arsenic-free antimony binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with gallium and sintered with LiF is described. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A lithium excess of 8 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. In a solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. Sintering at 1100 degrees C with a lithium excess of 8 mol% gives a relative density of 96% and a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using ethyl propionate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite-type having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. The suspension concentration is 8 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved sinterability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl propionate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. After heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. The Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and LGPS material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly.
