The Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The coating layer has an average thickness of 15 nm and a coverage of 85%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 50% relative to uncoated particles. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 40% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The LGPS and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li7P3S11, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. In an embodiment the material is Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. After heat treatment at 280 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 3.1 mS/cm. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours, and wherein the content of Li2O is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The silicon content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 20 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 3.1 mS/cm or more. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the sinterability are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.1 mS/cm or more.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium metal layer, a ceramic ion conductor layer, and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1 mA/cm2. The additive comprises indium in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LATP and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The method prevents short circuit and improves the sinterability and grain boundary resistance without a thick protective layer.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the content of the indium additive is 0.1 wt% to 5 wt%.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ceramic ion conductor containing a thio-LISICON phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing GeS2. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The content of GeS2 is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the moisture stability is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 75%, and wherein the content of GeS2 is 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Dendrite-suppressing magnesium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and lithium battery
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The additive content is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, the stack pressure is 5 MPa to 20 MPa, and the critical current density is 1 mA/cm2. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. A stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the electrochemical window is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3InCl6, Li6PS5Cl, and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 5 nm. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 80% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours. The arsenic-free antimony content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 4 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 3.1 mS/cm or more. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 4 cm3/g or less. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLZO, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 650 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tantalate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, Li2ZrO3, and LiF material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium fluoride (LiF). A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6, wherein z is 0.3 to 0.55, and a method for producing the same are provided. The LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein 0.3 <= z <= 0.55, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte by stirring the raw materials in acetonitrile at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in acetonitrile to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 100 degrees C to 280 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 300 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 85 degrees C.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Al2O3 layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ion-conductive solid. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A halide coating is compatible with the ion-conductive solid because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 500 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved electrochemical window and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition (Al2O3) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS material. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved cycle life and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 3.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite ion-conductive solid in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An ionic conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.2 to 1.6. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ion-conductive solid is improved. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 330 degrees C to 580 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein 1 <= a <= 1.8.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. The solid electrolyte may comprise lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 40 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed bromine-iodine substitution and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 11.2 mS/cm. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.45, and wherein 1.2 <= a <= 1.6, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more during cycling is described. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by uniaxial pressing. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide electrode layer pressed at 60 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a aluminum foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. Heat treatment at 550 degrees C after drying at 200 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for preparing the same
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 5 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the zirconium substitution and the surface region. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li2ZrO3 and LLTO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the solid-state battery. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The zirconium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the sinterability in contact with lithium.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for a solid-state lithium battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). In a solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.03, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less, and wherein 0.1 <= x <= 0.55.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Zirconium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ion-conductive solid with trigonal structure for lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ion-conductive solid with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. In the trigonal structure, yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. When z is 0.2, the conductivity is 3 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, LiF, and LiNbO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.2 V. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3InCl6. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 0.56 mS/cm or more. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a trigonal crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in 1,2-dimethoxyethane at 60 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ceramic ion conductor to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. The suspension concentration is 8 wt%, the reaction temperature is 60 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 180 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11. The ceramic ion conductor is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a ceramic ion conductor with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 3.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 0.5 wt% or less.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid by stirring the raw materials in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The ion-conductive solid may comprise argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 1 wt%. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 3.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide, and an initiator. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The membrane further contains a ceramic filler of Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet in an amount of 10 wt% to 30 wt% to form a composite electrolyte. The plasticizer succinonitrile is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The membrane of 20 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyacrylonitrile and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The 20 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm are obtained.
first_claim: 1. A polymer electrolyte membrane comprising: a polymer matrix comprising polyacrylonitrile; a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; and a plasticizer comprising succinonitrile in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt%, wherein the membrane has an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm or more at 40 degrees C.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Positive electrode active material with a gradient lithium niobate coating layer whose outer region contains lithium indium chloride
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide with a nickel content of 85 mol% or more and a gradient coating layer having an average thickness of 8 nm to 25 nm. The inner region of the coating layer adjacent to the core consists of amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the outer region contains lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) dispersed in the niobate so that the indium content increases continuously from 0 at% at the core to 15 at% to 30 at% at the outer surface. The coating layer is formed by applying a niobium alkoxide solution, heat-treating at 320 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and then applying an alcoholic solution of Li3InCl6 followed by vacuum drying. The niobate inner region blocks the formation of a space-charge layer and the diffusion of nickel into the sulfide, while the chloride-rich outer region, stable up to 4.3 V versus Li/Li+ and conductive to lithium ions, lowers the charge transfer resistance with Li6PS5Cl. The coverage is 92% or more and the interfacial resistance after 100 cycles at 4.3 V is 15 ohm cm2 or less. When the sulfide is a glass ceramic, the coated material further improves the high-voltage stability and interfacial resistance of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide in which nickel accounts for 85 mol% or more of transition metals; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and having an average thickness of 8 nm to 25 nm, the coating layer comprising an inner region adjacent to the core particles consisting of amorphous LiNbO3 and an outer region comprising Li3InCl6 dispersed in LiNbO3, wherein an indium content of the coating layer increases from 0 at% at the core particles to 15 at% to 30 at% at an outer surface of the coating layer.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by oxygen substitution is provided. The oxygen substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The ceramic ion conductor retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 10 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an oxygen substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from ethyl acetate, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the all-solid-state lithium battery. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.2 wt%. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by fibrillating a polytetrafluoroethylene binder and a solid-state battery including the sheet are described. The sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers, a porosity of 8%, a tensile strength of 1 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 120 degrees C to form a continuous film. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. No solvent is used in the process, so the ceramic ion conductor does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. A solid-state battery using the sheet shows improved ionic conductivity and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.6 MPa or more, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.3 V. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium fluoride (LiF). The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.1 V or more, and wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Nickel accounts for 60 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The LiNbO3, Li3InCl6, and Li2ZrO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The disclosure is applicable to lithium niobate (LiNbO3), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3) and has an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 40 nm to 200 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 300 cycles of stable plating and stripping. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The Li3PS4 and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The Li3N layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ceramic ion conductor. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 75 cycles or more, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.2 micrometers to 20 micrometers.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiTaO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm is provided. The Li2ZrO3 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The average thickness of the coating is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid in which part of the bromine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 3.5 mS/cm. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. In a solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ion-conductive solid whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. The Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 60% or more are obtained. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved moisture stability and sinterability and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: Provided is an electrode with a stainless steel current collector and a conductive primer layer that lowers the contact resistance with the electrode mixture layer. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 60 degrees C after lamination. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The positive electrode mixture layer contains the solid electrolyte, lithium iron phosphate, and a conductive agent. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 600 MPa. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The laminate is pressed by roll pressing at 600 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and method for preparing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Firing is performed at 500 degrees C for 2 hours to 10 hours in an argon atmosphere, which yields a conductivity of 6 mS/cm. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.15 or less. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the electrochemical window of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 50% to 85% by X-ray diffraction. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The solid electrolyte may comprise argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7P3S11. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant niobium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 1 mS/cm. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 2 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a relative density of 91% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a sintering temperature of 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a beta-Li3PS4 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing Li2O. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 1.2 mS/cm. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved ionic conductivity and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours, and wherein the content of Li2O is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tungstate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The Li2ZrO3 and Li3InCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 40 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.3 nm to 15 nm.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a lithium fluoride-containing additive layer
abstract: Provided is a solid-state cell in which lithium fluoride is added at the lithium metal interface in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% to suppress dendrites. The additive comprises lithium fluoride in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The LiF, Li3YCl6, and Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.7% after 100 cycles. The lithium fluoride additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and beta-Li3PS4. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the cycle life is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% or more, and wherein the content of the lithium fluoride additive is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 10 MPa to 40 MPa.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: Described is a combination of vinylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The passivation film on the positive electrode suppresses the dissolution of transition metals at 4.3 V. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.3 V. With 1 wt% of vinylene carbonate, the capacity retention after 500 cycles is 92% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 1 wt% of vinylene carbonate is also described. The additive vinylene carbonate is added in an amount of 1 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium hexafluorophosphate at a concentration of 1.5 M and vinylene carbonate as an additive.

title: Solvent-free free-standing solid electrolyte sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting solid electrolyte film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Because the fibril network holds the particles, the sheet is self-supporting and shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.8 MPa or more, and wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 30 degrees C to 90 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1.4 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 5.2 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The oxidation potential is 5.2 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 2 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the zirconium substitution and the surface region. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3, LLTO, and LLZO material. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 87% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 500 kPa
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 2 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar copper current collectors. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 2 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 50 micrometer separator layer. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 500 MPa.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 500 kPa or more.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using ethyl propionate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt%. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers. A solid-state battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1.
