A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The SiS2 addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 60% to 95%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic Ag-C layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 500 cycles of stable plating and stripping. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the solid electrolyte at the negative electrode is suppressed and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.2% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 50 nm to 3000 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 125 cycles or more.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: Described is a solvent-free film of a solid electrolyte with a fibril network that gives a tensile strength of 0.6 MPa or more. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The solid electrolyte powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The binder content is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, which gives a tensile strength of 1 MPa and a conductivity of 2 mS/cm. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.2 wt% to 1 wt%, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 10% or less, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.6 MPa or more.

title: Hafnium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ion-conductive solid stable above 4.8 V and lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.8 V. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. The oxide particles have a core of the perovskite-type LLTO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.49 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Solid electrolyte slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The solid content is 30 wt% to 50 wt%, the viscosity is 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the solid electrolyte, and the layer shows improved sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising anisole in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the solid content of the slurry is 30 wt% to 50 wt%, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. In a lithium secondary battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The suspension has a solid concentration of 7.5 wt% to 30 wt% and is reacted at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the reaction temperature is 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 3.1 mS/cm. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ion-conductive solid particles during pressing. The Li2O addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 20% to 100%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the content of Li2O is 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobium tantalum oxide, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The high coverage of the coating results in improved interfacial resistance at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 20% or more, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. Heat treatment at 450 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. The solvent is tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The oxygen substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The oxygen content of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 40 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 0.7 mS/cm or more. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the sinterability are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an oxygen substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with tungsten and sintered with LiF is described. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLTO and LATP material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. A sintering aid comprising LiF is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The grain size is 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and the relative density is 94% or more after sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the high-voltage stability of the garnet layer.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 0 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 1 micrometers to 60 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 900 degrees C to 1250 degrees C.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 45 degrees C. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The 1.0 M lithium hexafluorophosphate solution in ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more. With 2 wt% of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, the capacity retention after 300 cycles is 85% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.3 V. The non-aqueous electrolyte is injected into a lithium battery and the battery is stored at 45 degrees C. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.3 V.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium hexafluorophosphate; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate; and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite in an amount of 2 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide solid electrolyte that does not require long mechanical milling. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 1.5 mS/cm or more, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 5 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The content of GeS2 is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.8 mS/cm or more. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 320 degrees C. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), lithium niobate (LiNbO3), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the high-voltage stability is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 230 degrees C to 420 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the degree of crystallinity is 20% to 100%.

title: Single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte and lithium metal battery using the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene matrix, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide as the lithium salt, and succinonitrile as a plasticizer. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The plasticizer succinonitrile enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 60 degrees C. The polymer matrix is polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 16:1. The 50 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing a lithium battery, comprising: assembling a positive electrode, a separator, and a negative electrode; injecting a composition comprising a monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and an initiator; and polymerizing the composition in situ to form a gel polymer electrolyte.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention at 45 degrees C is improved by an additive combination. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery in which the electrolyte contains the additive combination. The additive lithium difluorophosphate is added in an amount of 1 wt% based on the total weight of the electrolyte. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. With 1 wt% of lithium difluorophosphate, the capacity retention after 500 cycles is 88% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The stable passivation film formed by lithium difluorophosphate suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate; and lithium difluorophosphate in an amount of 1 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The solvent is a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A precursor of the Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and LLZO material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 5 wt% to 20 wt%, and wherein the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 5 mS/cm. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 and LLZO material. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The Li7P3S11 and LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 4 wt% to 16 wt%.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% and a viscosity of 3000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 30 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The binder is polyisobutylene in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent xylene. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a binder content of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 16 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar nickel-plated copper current collectors. The current collector of nickel-plated copper is used in a lithium battery with a 20 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The laminate is pressed by uniaxial pressing at 100 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a nickel-plated copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 100 kPa or more.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ceramic ion conductor with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and production method thereof
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which hydrolysis is suppressed by tin substitution is provided. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The substitution amount is 5 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.7 mS/cm or more. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved moisture stability and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours is 70% or more, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte and to a lithium battery including the same. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The total ionic conductivity is 0.42 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Al2O3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 0.2 micrometers to 12 micrometers, and wherein 0.11 <= v <= 0.8, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1000 degrees C to 1350 degrees C.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Bromine-substituted Li6PS5X solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm. The low electronic conductivity of the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The mixed halogen substitution improves the electrochemical window and moisture stability of the all-solid-state battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.2 <= x <= 0.65, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and to a method of handling it in a dry room. After exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity retention is 90%. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 5 cm3/g. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The LLZO, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and ionic conductivity and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours is 65% or more.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 11.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The ceramic ion conductor provides improved ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein 1.2 <= a <= 1.6, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 8.4 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for preparing the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.1, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material is used in an all-solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The mixed halogen substitution improves the moisture stability of the all-solid-state lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, and wherein 0.3 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium metal layer, a ceramic ion conductor layer, and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99.3% after 100 cycles. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the solid-state battery. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The Li3PS4, LLZO, and Li3YCl6 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved cycle life and dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising indium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 1.4 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 98.8% or more.

assignee_std: CORAST INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tungstate and to a method for producing the same. The coating layer has an average thickness of 8 nm and a coverage of 80%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 30% relative to uncoated particles. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. An all-solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12 and Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A lithium excess of 10 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. A solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The grain size is 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and the relative density is 91% or more after sintering at 1020 degrees C to 1170 degrees C. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The low grain boundary resistance results in improved ionic conductivity compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 0.5 micrometers to 30 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a relative density of 86% or more.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more during cycling is described. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 300 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. A lithium battery pack comprising 16 modules of the stacked cells is also described. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 80 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 50 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 300 kPa.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The ion-conductive solid may comprise beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 85% after humid exposure. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 6 hours is 75% or more.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ion-conductive solid in the all-solid-state battery. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 50 nm. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression of the lithium metal battery.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising silver-carbon composite (Ag-C) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.8% or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A wet film of an ion-conductive solid cast on a PET release film and dried in an oven is described. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The solid content is 50 wt% to 70 wt%, the viscosity is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s, and the layer thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The wet film is dried at 120 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The ion-conductive solid is a lithium ion conducting material for an all-solid-state battery. The nonpolar solvent does not degrade the ion-conductive solid, and the layer shows improved interfacial resistance and sheet formability.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; a polyisobutylene binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the viscosity of the slurry at 25 degrees C is 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a solid electrolyte of high conductivity. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The Li3PS4, LGPS, and Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 12 hours, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming an ion-conductive solid film without any solvent. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The sheet thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, the porosity is 10% or less, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. No solvent is used in the process, so the ion-conductive solid does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the sheet shows improved ionic conductivity and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 10% or less, and wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C.

title: Electrolyte for a lithium ion battery operable at low temperature and method of preparing the same
abstract: Described is a combination of lithium difluorophosphate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.4 V. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The solid electrolyte interphase on the silicon particles accommodates the volume change. The electrolyte further contains a fluorinated ether as a co-solvent to improve the oxidation stability at 4.4 V. The 1.5 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode, a separator, and the non-aqueous electrolyte is also provided. The 1.5 M lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide solution in propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate keeps a conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more.
first_claim: 1. A non-aqueous electrolyte solution for a lithium secondary battery, comprising: a lithium salt comprising lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide; a non-aqueous solvent comprising propylene carbonate and dimethyl carbonate; and lithium difluorophosphate in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% based on a total weight of the electrolyte solution.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed bromine-iodine substitution for lithium battery
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiBr and Li3PS4. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 500 degrees C. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.3 or less, and wherein 0.05 <= y/a <= 0.55.

title: Lithium sulfide based cathode active material with suppressed polysulfide dissolution
abstract: Disclosed is a composite cathode in which iron sulfide is confined in the pores of carbon nanotubes to suppress the dissolution of polysulfides. A lithium secondary battery comprising the positive electrode, a lithium-containing negative electrode, and an electrolyte is also provided. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the iron sulfide cathode. The iron sulfide is melt-diffused into carbon nanotubes at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. The capacity retention after 100 cycles is 90% at 25 degrees C. The carbon coating on the iron sulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 90%.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a lithium-sulfur battery, comprising: a porous carbon comprising carbon nanotubes; iron sulfide impregnated in pores of the porous carbon in an amount of 60 wt% to 80 wt%; and a carbon coating layer having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm on a surface of the porous carbon.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 200 nm. The protective layer thickness is 80 nm to 400 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.8% or more. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.8% or more, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 10 mol%. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. Sintering at 1200 degrees C with a lithium excess of 10 mol% gives a relative density of 97% and a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO and LLZO material. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 25 mol%, and wherein 0.21 <= v <= 0.9.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO ion-conductive solid in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The oxide particles have a core of the perovskite-type LLTO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 83% or more. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 83% or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.7 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which solid electrolyte particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and the sheet shows a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the all-solid-state lithium battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The method shortens the process and improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity of the layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.4 wt% to 2 wt%, and wherein the free-standing solid electrolyte sheet has a roll temperature of 90 degrees C to 150 degrees C, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a zinc-containing additive layer
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 2.1 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state lithium battery. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 3 mA/cm2. A stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and Li3YCl6. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. In a solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The negative electrode structure gives a higher critical current density and improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising zinc dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 99% or more.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Solid electrolyte sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Disclosed is a solvent-free method of forming a solid electrolyte sheet by kneading the powder with PTFE under shear and rolling the mixture between heated rollers. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and beta-Li3PS4, and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. With a binder content of 3 wt% and a roll temperature of 120 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 20% or less. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LATP and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A solid-state lithium battery using the sheet shows improved ionic conductivity and a thinner electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the thickness of the sheet is 32 micrometers to 160 micrometers, and wherein the porosity of the sheet is 20% or less, and wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 1.8 MPa or more.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% after 100 cycles. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), beta-Li3PS4, and Li3YCl6. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 300 nm. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 120 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiPON layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: This disclosure concerns a protective layer comprising a LiPON inorganic layer and a fluorinated polymer for a lithium metal negative electrode. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The LiPON layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the ion-conductive solid. The inorganic layer is formed by thermal evaporation to a thickness of 80 nm to 400 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 1 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% and no dendrite penetration is observed. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved interfacial resistance and dendrite suppression.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 80 nm to 400 nm.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for preparing the same
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. A solid-state battery comprising the LLTO and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the grain boundary resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 80% or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte comprises dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension, reacting the suspension to form a solvate complex precipitate, and removing the solvent. In a solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The solid electrolyte is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the solid-state lithium battery. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives a solid electrolyte with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 160 degrees C to 240 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 5 wt% to 20 wt%.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tungsten stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The sintered body has a relative density of 92%, an average grain size of 10 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has an average grain size of 1 micrometers to 60 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ion-conductive solid has a lithium excess of 10 mol% to 30 mol%, and wherein 0.06 <= v <= 0.75.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li7P3S11 phase for lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. The Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a Li7P3S11 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm.
