Heat treatment at 300 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 0.84 mS/cm or more. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF material. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using tetrahydrofuran for lithium battery
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO, Li7P3S11, and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 180 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. Dissolution and precipitation give a homogeneous composition and improved moisture stability and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C is 2.9 mS/cm or more.

title: Slurry composition for a solid electrolyte layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-butadiene rubber
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming a solid electrolyte layer. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The ion-conductive component may be Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 30 micrometers. The LGPS, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The LGPS, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; a styrene-butadiene rubber binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers, and wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 100 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the ionic conductivity of the layer at 25 degrees C is 0.8 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers. The solid electrolyte is preferably lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.4 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 73% or more.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium scandium bromide solid electrolyte with monoclinic structure and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Br6, wherein z is 0.2 to 0.45, and a method for producing the same are provided. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2WO4 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. The Li3InCl6 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The ion-conductive solid powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) and has an average thickness of 2 nm to 10 nm and a coverage of 90% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 90% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 2 nm to 10 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by bromine. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein 1.2 <= a <= 1.6.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass solid electrolyte containing a thio-LISICON phase and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 5 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 3.1 mS/cm. The LGPS material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of LiI is 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 360 degrees C, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 4 hours.

title: Tin-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ion-conductive solid stable above 5.2 V and production method thereof
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ion-conductive solid with an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more is described. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A lithium battery using the oxide shows improved grain boundary resistance at a charging voltage of 4.6 V.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by tin; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.9 V or more, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ceramic ion conductor. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. With the additive in an amount of 0.5 wt% and a stack pressure of 10 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99.3%. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The lithium fluoride additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the ionic conductivity is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising lithium fluoride dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2 MPa to 50 MPa, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.8% or more, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 200 cycles or more.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tantalum-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 92% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The ceramic ion conductor is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The total ionic conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the grain boundary resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 87% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 1 micrometers to 60 micrometers.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. An all-solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y), wherein 1.3 <= a <= 1.7, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by cold isostatic pressing
abstract: A pressure jig that applies a uniform stack pressure of 500 kPa to a laminated cell and a method of using the jig are provided. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by cold isostatic pressing. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a copper current collector is also provided. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 500 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. A solid electrolyte sheet of 30 micrometers is used as the separator.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by cold isostatic pressing at 500 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the content of SiS2 is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and zirconium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.3 V. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6 and LiF material. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein 0 <= z <= 0.7, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.32 mS/cm or more.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3YCl6 and method for producing the same
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3YCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The coated particles are heat-treated at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li2ZrO3 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 180 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.8 nm to 40 nm.

title: Lithium nitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% and no dendrite penetration is observed. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 100 nm. The bilayer structure improves the interfacial resistance and dendrite suppression compared with a single inorganic layer.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.2% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 10 nm to 600 nm.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state battery is described. A precursor of the Li2ZrO3, Li3InCl6, and LiNbO3 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The coating layer has an average thickness of 5 nm and a coverage of 95%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. A halide phase of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type having a trigonal or monoclinic structure is also formed, and its composition is adjusted by yttrium or indium substitution. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium niobate (LiNbO3), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 0.5 nm to 25 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and a porosity of 10% or less is provided. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The fibril network occupies 1 vol% to 5 vol% of the sheet, and the remainder is the ion-conductive particles. The roll temperature is 50 degrees C to 110 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers after calendering. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The dry sheet is useful as a separator layer for roll-to-roll production, with improved interfacial resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet, comprising: solid electrolyte particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the tensile strength of the sheet is 0.3 MPa or more, and wherein the thickness of the sheet is 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1 mA/cm2. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The Li3YCl6, LLZO, and LiF material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a Coulombic efficiency of 97.5% or more, and wherein the content of the magnesium additive is 0.05 wt% to 2.5 wt%, and wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2 MPa to 50 MPa.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for a lithium secondary battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y). Suitable compositions include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.12 or less. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The site occupancy of iodine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The Li6PS5X phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the iodine-substituted Li6PS5X shows a higher conductivity and better ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein 1.3 <= a <= 1.7, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. The halogen-rich composition keeps the Li6PS5X phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having a Li6PS5X crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein 1.2 <= a <= 1.6.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and method for producing the same
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The polymer layer comprises polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and has a thickness of 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. A cell with the protected lithium metal negative electrode operates for 300 cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved interfacial resistance. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The LiF layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the solid electrolyte at the negative electrode is suppressed and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 98.5% or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 120 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers.

title: Solvent-free free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet with fibrillated PTFE binder
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ion-conductive solid particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The sheet has a thickness of 20 micrometers, a porosity of 10%, a tensile strength of 2 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The method further comprises a synthesis step in which a solvate complex is precipitated and heat-treated to obtain the powder. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the ionic conductivity and sheet formability of the cell.
first_claim: 1. A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet, comprising: ion-conductive solid particles; and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network binding the particles without a solvent, wherein the ionic conductivity of the sheet at 25 degrees C is 0.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of the fibrillated binder is 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet has a roll temperature of 20 degrees C to 180 degrees C.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3YCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 8 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. The LiNbO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiNbO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium yttrium chloride (Li3YCl6), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 75% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 75 mol% or more.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ceramic ion conductor with orthorhombic structure and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. In the orthorhombic structure, yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the moisture stability at 4.3 V is improved.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 80 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.6 mS/cm or more.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ion-conductive solid using 1,2-dimethoxyethane for lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less. The solvent is 1,2-dimethoxyethane, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl material. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The ion-conductive solid obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt%. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 70 degrees C to 250 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 1 wt% to 32 wt%, and wherein the residual solvent content is 1.5 wt% or less, and wherein the reaction temperature is 0 degrees C to 120 degrees C.

title: Lithium ion battery electrolyte with improved high temperature storage characteristics
abstract: Disclosed is an electrolyte additive, tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, that forms a stable passivation film on the negative electrode and suppresses gas generation. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is compatible with a silicon-containing negative electrode. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M in a mixed solvent of ethylene carbonate and diethyl carbonate in a volume ratio of 3:7. Also provided is a lithium secondary battery whose capacity retention after 500 cycles is 92% with the electrolyte. The 1.2 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The stable passivation film formed by tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles.
first_claim: 1. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode, a negative electrode comprising graphite and silicon, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte, wherein the non-aqueous electrolyte comprises lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide at a concentration of 1.2 M and tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite as an additive.

title: Planar solid oxide fuel cell stack with metal interconnects and a glass sealant
abstract: This disclosure concerns a tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte and a nickel cermet anode. The electrolyte layer has a thickness of 8 micrometers and a relative density of 95%, and the open circuit voltage is 1.1 V at 500 to 650 degrees C. The electrolyte layer is formed by tape casting and co-sintering at 1300 to 1400 degrees C with the anode support, which gives a relative density of 95%. The co-sintering process at 1300 to 1400 degrees C reduces the number of firing steps and the manufacturing cost of the lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite cell. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 8 micrometers. The thin 8 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 1.5 W/cm2.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell comprising: a porous anode support comprising nickel and a ceramic; an electrolyte layer disposed on the anode support and comprising lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite, the electrolyte layer having a thickness of 8 micrometers or less; a barrier layer comprising doped ceria disposed on the electrolyte layer; and a cathode comprising lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite disposed on the barrier layer.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 1 hours. The ion-conductive component may be Li7P3S11. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -20 degrees C is 2 cm3/g. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 1 hours. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 350 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an oxygen substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 1 hours is 60% or more.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and production method thereof
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. A solid-state battery comprising the LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the solid-state battery. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the electrochemical window and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.5 hours to 20 hours, and wherein the content of P2O5 is 4 mol% to 16 mol%.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a nickel-plated copper current collector and a primer layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 20 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by roll pressing and the release film is peeled. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 8 cells and a case is also provided. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 100 MPa. The roll pressing step at 100 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The module with 8 stacked cells has a voltage of 8 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L. The current collector is a nickel-plated copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm and a retention of 80% after humid exposure. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved moisture stability and sinterability and simpler handling.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 2 hours is 55% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.9 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a silicon substitution amount of 1 mol% to 20 mol%.

title: Amperometric carbon dioxide sensor using an oxide ion conducting ceramic and gas sensor system
abstract: An exhaust gas sensor with a pumping cell, a sensing cell, and a diffusion controlling portion is described. The solid electrolyte layer is a dense ceramic sintered at 1400 degrees C. The reference electrode is exposed to atmospheric air through a channel in the laminated body. The sensor shows a response time of 20 seconds to a step change of carbon dioxide concentration at 700 degrees C. The auxiliary electrode comprises sodium carbonate and is in contact with both the ceramic and the gas. The built-in heater shortens the warm-up time of the sensor to 700 degrees C. The sensor with a response time of 20 seconds can monitor a lithium battery manufacturing line for carbon dioxide. The sensor operating at 700 degrees C has a detection limit of 1 ppm for carbon dioxide.
first_claim: 1. A mixed potential type gas sensor comprising a zirconia ceramic, a first electrode comprising a metal oxide, and a second electrode comprising platinum, wherein a potential difference between the first electrode and the second electrode depends on a concentration of carbon dioxide.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more during cycling is described. The electrode laminate pressed at 600 MPa and 60 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The current collector of nickel-plated copper is used in a lithium battery with a 100 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The primer layer on the nickel-plated copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa through an elastic sheet. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The separator layer is a sheet of 100 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A battery module comprising a laminated cell, a pair of end plates, an elastic sheet disposed between the cell and one of the end plates, and bolts connecting the end plates, wherein the end plates apply a stack pressure of 600 kPa or more to the cell.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The halide shows an activation energy of 0.35 eV or less and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, YBr3, and ZrBr4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which yttrium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein 0.2 <= z <= 0.45, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7P3S11, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The suspension concentration is 5 wt%, the reaction temperature is 25 degrees C, and the drying temperature is 120 degrees C. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in 1,2-dimethoxyethane to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 2.5 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Provided is a sulfide solid electrolyte that retains 70% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 70% or more are obtained. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4. The tin substitution amount is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the sinterability and grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours is 55% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.8 V. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and wherein the oxide solid electrolyte has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 80% or more.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium indium chloride ion-conductive solid with orthorhombic structure and method for preparing the same
abstract: A halide ion-conductive solid comprises an orthorhombic crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6. The median particle diameter D50 is 1 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 2.1 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.3 micrometers to 3 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Zr(z)Cl6; and a close-packed chloride anion sublattice in which indium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C, and wherein 0.02 <= z <= 0.25, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium scandium bromide ceramic ion conductor with monoclinic structure and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The oxidation stability limit is 4.3 V or more and the conductivity is 1.05 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, ScBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a monoclinic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Ti(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which scandium and titanium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein 0.1 <= z <= 0.35, and wherein the halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.05 mS/cm or more.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y) and to an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the same. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 11.2 mS/cm. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.075 or less. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The solid electrolyte provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein 0.05 <= y/a <= 0.55.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and solid-state lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium tungstate and to a method for producing the same. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. A solid-state lithium battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and nickel content of 80 mol% or more. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4) and has an average thickness of 1.2 nm to 6 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tungstate (Li2WO4), wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.2 nm to 6 nm, and wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 80% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 80 mol% or more.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition for lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as a 5 V spinel. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved grain boundary resistance. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 80%. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the grain boundary resistance of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a capacity retention after 200 cycles of 75% or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.7 V or more.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an arsenic-free antimony-rich surface region is described. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 24 hours is 60% or more.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). The argyrodite-type phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 6 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.24 or less, and wherein 0.1 <= y/a <= 0.6.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite-type structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.15 or less. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein 1.2 <= a <= 1.6, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic argyrodite-type structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 480 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved moisture stability and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.15 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 4.5 mS/cm or more.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
