title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder and lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-iodine substitution. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.045 or less. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the cycle life of the material is retained after storage.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a firing temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less, and wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.45.

title: Air-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 10 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours is 80% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a heat treatment temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less.

title: Anode-supported solid oxide fuel cell having a thin lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte layer and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a solid oxide fuel cell in which a thin lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte is co-sintered with an anode support to lower the ohmic resistance of the cell. The cell operates at 500 to 650 degrees C with a power density of 1.5 W/cm2 and shows thermal cycling durability of 50 cycles. The reversible cell with a lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte and the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate. The cathode comprises barium strontium cobalt ferrite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified. A 8 micrometer solid electrolyte reduces the ohmic loss of the solid oxide fuel cell. The cell can be operated at 500 to 650 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects.
first_claim: 1. A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising a plurality of planar unit cells each having an anode, an electrolyte layer comprising lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite and a cathode, metal interconnects disposed between adjacent unit cells, and a glass sealant, wherein the stack operates at 500 to 650 degrees C.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide solid electrolyte having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The solid electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state battery without a drying step. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material is useful as a solid electrolyte layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and electrochemical window.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein 0.35 <= y/a <= 0.65, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a firing temperature of 430 degrees C to 530 degrees C.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: An air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid in which hydrolysis is suppressed by silicon substitution is provided. The silicon substitution amount is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by silicon; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 24 hours is 75% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a silicon substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 20 cm3/g or less.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Specific examples are Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 2.6 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better cycle life and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.6 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.045 or less, and wherein 0.3 <= x <= 0.75.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is a ceramic ion conductor comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. Also described is an all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved interfacial resistance and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.3 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C, and wherein the content of LiI is 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Oxygen-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 10 cm3/g or less. The oxygen content of 4 mol% to 16 mol% suppresses H2S generation to 10 cm3/g or less while the conductivity remains 3.1 mS/cm or more. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an oxygen substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Bromine-substituted argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery
abstract: A ceramic ion conductor comprising a crystal phase of the argyrodite-type type is provided, wherein the halogen site is occupied by both chlorine and bromine. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ceramic ion conductor exhibits an ionic conductivity of 4.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an activation energy of 0.28 eV or less. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.12 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 3.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein 1.3 <= a <= 1.7.

title: Halide solid electrolyte having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide solid electrolyte of scandium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.2 V. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. When z is 0.1, the conductivity is 3 mS/cm and the electrochemical window extends to 4.2 V. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.02 to 0.25 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide solid electrolyte, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Sc(1-z)Hf(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which scandium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C, and wherein the halide solid electrolyte has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4 V or more.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite-type family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. Specific examples are argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the bromine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite-type crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a firing temperature of 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.45, and wherein 1.4 <= a <= 1.8.

title: Gallium-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and lithium battery
abstract: A garnet solid electrolyte sintered body having an average grain size of 8 micrometers and a low grain boundary resistance is provided. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state lithium battery. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1200 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm and a relative density of 94%. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. Suitable compositions include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Sintering is performed at 1200 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Ga(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein 0.05 <= v <= 0.4, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.42 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a lithium excess of 5 mol% to 13 mol%.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. An all-solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The suspension has a solid concentration of 5 wt% to 20 wt% and is reacted at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The method does not require long mechanical milling and gives an ion-conductive solid with improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C, and wherein the drying temperature under vacuum is 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. Partial substitution of chlorine with bromine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm after cold pressing at 370 MPa. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x), wherein 0.3 <= x <= 0.75, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 5.5 mS/cm or more.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by uniaxial pressing at 300 MPa and 60 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The uniaxial pressing step at 300 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The unit cells are stacked 8 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. A lithium battery module comprising the laminate and a copper current collector is also provided. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 8 cells and a case is also provided.
first_claim: 1. A battery cell comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, a separator layer disposed therebetween, and an edge sealing portion of an insulating resin surrounding the positive electrode layer, wherein the separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO ion-conductive solid in which hafnium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The oxidation potential is 5.2 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a perovskite-type LLTO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ion-conductive solid has a substitution amount of 0.4 mol% to 8 mol%.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li3BO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li3BO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. Suitable compositions include lithium niobate (LiNbO3), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The average thickness of the coating is 2 nm to 10 nm, the coverage is 85% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 75 mol% or more of the transition metals. The LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The lithium borate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 280 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 55 mol% or more, and wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 5% or more.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a thio-LISICON phase and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-Li2O glass. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. The material comprises Li7P3S11 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the electrochemical window is retained.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 60% to 95%, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1.8 mS/cm or more, and wherein the sulfide ceramic ion conductor has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C.

title: Densified garnet oxide ceramic ion conductor and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant aluminum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The total ionic conductivity is 0.84 mS/cm or more and the grain boundary resistance is 20% or less of the total resistance. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The dopant aluminum occupies the zirconium or lithium site in an amount v of 0.05 to 0.4, which stabilizes the cubic garnet phase. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. A sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a sintering temperature of 1170 degrees C to 1320 degrees C, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 92% or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The Li6PS5Cl, LGPS, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The ion-conductive solid shows improved ionic conductivity compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 2.2 mS/cm or more, and wherein the content of Li2O is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the sulfide ion-conductive solid has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 220 degrees C to 300 degrees C.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a tin-rich surface region is described. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Examples of the ion conductor include Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and LATP composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1.5 mS/cm. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -20 degrees C and the exposure time is 24 hours. The tin substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. An all-solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by tin; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 1 mS/cm or more, and wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C for 24 hours is 80% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a tin substitution amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 15 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The Li3InCl6 and LiNbO3 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The lithium tantalate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium tantalate (LiTaO3), wherein the reduction of interfacial resistance relative to uncoated particles is 25% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 50 mol% or more, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 1.5 nm to 75 nm.

title: Niobium-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and method for producing the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ceramic ion conductor doped with niobium and sintered with Li3BO3 is described. The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the densification is achieved by hot pressing at 10 MPa to 50 MPa. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Nb(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising Li3BO3 present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has a relative density of 92% or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Br6 and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide ion-conductive solid in which erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. After dehydration under vacuum at 200 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the high-voltage stability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A halide ion-conductive solid, comprising: an orthorhombic crystal phase of a metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Zr(z)Br6; and a close-packed bromide anion sublattice in which erbium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites, wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.56 mS/cm or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has an oxidation stability limit versus Li/Li+ of 4.3 V or more, and wherein the halide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C.

title: Tungsten-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a tungsten-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 94% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. When v is 0.25, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1.2 mS/cm. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte, comprising: a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)W(v)O12; and a sintering aid comprising LiF present at grain boundaries, wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.84 mS/cm or more, and wherein the garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte has a sintering temperature of 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. A precursor of the Li7P3S11, Li3PS4, and LATP material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. After exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C for 1 hours, the conductivity retention is 80%. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 40 cm3/g or less, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment temperature of 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide solid electrolyte has an arsenic-free antimony substitution amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%.

title: Lithium borate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3BO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium borate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3), wherein the coverage of the coating layer determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy is 85% or more, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated therein. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3YCl6, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium fluoride (LiF). The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li7P3S11 phase precipitates uniformly. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The Li2O addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 40% to 100%, and wherein the content of Li2O is 1.6 mol% to 32 mol%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a heat treatment time of 0.1 hours to 40 hours.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 300 kPa
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 300 kPa or more during cycling is described. The negative electrode layer of the lithium battery comprises graphite and is pressed at 300 MPa. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 300 kPa. The primer layer on the aluminum foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The unit cells are stacked 16 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 30 micrometer separator layer. The separator layer is a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing.
first_claim: 1. A method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for a battery, comprising: forming a positive electrode layer comprising lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide on a current collector; placing an electrolyte sheet having a thickness of 30 micrometers on the positive electrode layer; placing a negative electrode layer on the electrolyte sheet; and pressing the laminate by roll pressing at 300 MPa and 80 degrees C.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a Li7P3S11 phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing LiI. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The LiI addition suppresses devitrification to low-conductivity phases and improves the cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a glass phase comprising Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 80:20; and a Li7P3S11 crystal phase precipitated in the glass phase, wherein the degree of crystallinity is 50% to 85%, and wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a crystallization heat treatment temperature of 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C, and wherein the content of LiI is 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.

assignee_std: QILUNHE NEW ENERGY TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
title: Dendrite-suppressing magnesium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 2.8 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. The additive layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 5 micrometers and is lithiophilic. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LATP and LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The additive content is 2 wt% to 10 wt%, the stack pressure is 1 MPa to 4 MPa, and the critical current density is 4 mA/cm2. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a ceramic ion conductor layer; and an additive comprising magnesium dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 2.8 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the content of the magnesium additive is 2 wt% to 10 wt%, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 250 cycles or more.

title: Hafnium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ceramic ion conductor stable above 4.8 V and lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LATP material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.8 V. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less.

title: Lithium fluoride-rich halide interlayer protecting a lithium metal negative electrode from a sulfide solid electrolyte
abstract: A protective interlayer disposed between a lithium metal negative electrode and a sulfide solid electrolyte layer comprises a lithium fluoride-rich halide composition represented by Li(3-w)Y(1-w)Cl(6-6w)F(6w), wherein 0.1 <= w <= 0.3, in which fluoride partially replaces chloride so that the halide is thermodynamically stable against metallic lithium while retaining an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. The interlayer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers and is formed by casting a slurry of the halide powder and a fluorinated binder onto the lithium foil, or by applying a halide coating of the composition to the surface of the sulfide solid electrolyte layer facing the negative electrode. A thin LiF-rich passivation film of 5 nm to 30 nm forms spontaneously at the lithium side upon first contact and blocks electron leakage, so that the reductive decomposition of the sulfide solid electrolyte is suppressed and the electrochemical window of the cell is extended on the reduction side to 0 V. A lithium metal cell comprising the interlayer shows an interfacial resistance of 15 ohm cm2 or less and operates for 400 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 without short circuit.
first_claim: 1. An interlayer for a lithium metal cell, disposed between a lithium metal negative electrode and a sulfide solid electrolyte layer, the interlayer comprising a halide composition represented by Li(3-w)Y(1-w)Cl(6-6w)F(6w), wherein 0.1 <= w <= 0.3, wherein the interlayer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers and an ionic conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.5 V or more is described. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. With hafnium substitution of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The positive electrode active material is LiCoPO4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. The widened electrochemical window improves the ionic conductivity of a high-voltage lithium battery.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by hafnium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity at 25 degrees C of 0.7 mS/cm or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.5 V or more.

assignee_std: SEODAM NATIONAL UNIVERSITY INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into an ion-conductive solid layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. The inorganic layer is formed by thermal evaporation to a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4. The bilayer with a total thickness of 1 micrometer gives 300 cycles of stable plating and stripping. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ion-conductive solid at the negative electrode is suppressed and the interfacial resistance is improved.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium phosphorus oxynitride (LiPON) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 100 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.8% or more.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa with a silver additive. The additive particles have a size of 200 nm and the critical current density rises from 0.6 mA/cm2 to 1 mA/cm2. The silver additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising a solid electrolyte, comprising: a lithium metal layer; a solid electrolyte layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the solid electrolyte layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a critical current density at 25 degrees C of 0.4 mA/cm2 or more, and wherein the content of the silver additive is 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Ceramic ion conductor slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: A method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The binder content of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt% gives a peel strength of 0.1 N/cm or more and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. The LiF and Li3YCl6 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% to 80 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A precursor of the LiF and Li3YCl6 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. Because the binder is dissolved in the solvent, the layer is uniform and shows improved cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer, comprising: ceramic ion conductor particles; a styrene-ethylene-butylene-styrene block copolymer binder; a nonpolar solvent comprising heptane in which the binder is dissolved; and a dispersant, wherein the slurry has a drying temperature of 40 degrees C to 140 degrees C, and wherein the thickness of the dried layer is 5 micrometers to 100 micrometers.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid arsenic-free antimony binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 2 cm3/g. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm. The Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the sinterability are improved.
first_claim: 1. A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony; and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element, wherein the conductivity retention after exposure to air having a dew point of -40 degrees C for 2 hours is 60% or more, and wherein the moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid has a heat treatment temperature of 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, and wherein the cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes is 4 cm3/g or less.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ion-conductive solid powder
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in ethyl acetate to give a sulfide ion-conductive solid precursor. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state battery. A precursor of the Li7P3S11 and Li6PS5Cl material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the sinterability and moisture stability.
first_claim: 1. A method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid, the method comprising: dispersing Li2S and P2S5 in ethyl acetate to form a suspension; reacting the suspension at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring to form a solvate complex precipitate; removing the solvent at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure; and heat-treating the dried precipitate at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, wherein the reaction temperature is 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C, and wherein the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, and wherein the solid concentration of the suspension is 7.5 wt% to 30 wt%.

title: Solid-state battery cell with an edge sealing portion and battery module including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium cobalt oxide positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The cold isostatic pressing step at 200 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The electrode laminate pressed at 200 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The unit cells are stacked 2 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The separator layer is a sheet of 50 micrometers thickness transferred from a release film by pressing. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The laminate of 2 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The structure with the copper current collector is applied to an all-solid-state battery for a vehicle.
first_claim: 1. A stacked battery comprising: a plurality of unit cells each comprising a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer; and bipolar current collectors each comprising a copper foil and disposed between adjacent unit cells, wherein the unit cells are stacked in series and the stack is pressed at 200 kPa or more.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for a lithium secondary battery has an argyrodite crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. When fired at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11, wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. Specific examples are beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11. The mixed halogen substitution improves the electrochemical window of the lithium secondary battery.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide solid electrolyte, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y), wherein the sulfide solid electrolyte has a peak intensity ratio IA/IB of 0.075 or less, and wherein 0.15 <= y/a <= 0.45, and wherein 1.3 <= a <= 1.7.

title: Lithium fluoride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by thermal evaporation. The inorganic layer is formed by thermal evaporation to a thickness of 120 nm to 600 nm and has an ionic conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm or more at 25 degrees C. After 300 cycles at 0.5 mA/cm2 the cell retains a Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% and no dendrite penetration is observed. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The Li3InCl6 and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the solid-state lithium battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. The polymer layer keeps the contact during volume change and improves the high-voltage stability and cycle life.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium fluoride (LiF) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 120 nm to 600 nm, and wherein the protective layer has an average Coulombic efficiency over 100 cycles of 97.8% or more.

assignee_std: UNIVERSITY OF SELEXEN INDUSTRY-ACADEMIC COOPERATION FOUNDATION
title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved ionic conductivity and Coulombic efficiency.
first_claim: 1. A protective layer for a lithium metal negative electrode, comprising: an inorganic layer comprising lithium nitride (Li3N) in contact with the lithium metal; and a fluorine-containing polymer layer disposed on the inorganic layer, wherein the number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more, and wherein the thickness of the protective layer is 20 nm to 100 nm, and wherein the thickness of the polymer layer is 1 micrometers to 6 micrometers.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and lithium battery
abstract: A NASICON-type or perovskite-type oxide ceramic ion conductor with an oxidation limit of 4.9 V or more is described. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The decomposition current density at 5 V is 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less and the capacity retention after 200 cycles is 75% or more. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the high-voltage stability of the electrolyte layer.
first_claim: 1. An oxide ceramic ion conductor, comprising: a NASICON-type LATP phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium; and an oxidation-resistant surface region having a thickness of 5 nm to 50 nm, wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a decomposition current density at 5 V of 4 microamperes per square centimeter or less, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has an oxidation potential versus Li/Li+ of 4.9 V or more, and wherein the oxide ceramic ion conductor has a substitution amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a silver-containing additive layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to the suppression of lithium filament growth in a solid-state cell by an additive that promotes uniform plating and stripping. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 4 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 300 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. A stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The suppression of void formation improves the ionic conductivity during fast charging.
first_claim: 1. A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid, comprising: a lithium metal layer; an ion-conductive solid layer; and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ion-conductive solid layer to form uniform nucleation sites, wherein the negative electrode structure has a stack pressure of 2 MPa to 50 MPa, and wherein the number of plating and stripping cycles without short circuit is 60 cycles or more, and wherein the content of the silver additive is 0.2 wt% to 10 wt%.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2ZrO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2ZrO3 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved interfacial resistance and high-voltage stability.
first_claim: 1. A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: core particles comprising a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide; and a coating layer disposed on a surface of the core particles and comprising an amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), wherein the positive electrode active material has a heat treatment temperature of 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C, and wherein the average thickness of the coating layer is 6 nm to 30 nm, and wherein the positive electrode active material has a nickel content among transition metals of 70 mol% or more.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), wherein the argyrodite crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The argyrodite crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The ion-conductive solid provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.
first_claim: 1. A sulfide ion-conductive solid, comprising: a crystal phase having an argyrodite crystal structure; and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y), wherein 0.25 <= y/a <= 0.75.

assignee_std: HWASEOL NATIONAL RESEARCH INSTITUTE OF ENERGY MATERIALS
title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The solvent is a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and Li3InCl6. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, LiNbO3, and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided.
